stories.title: Meerut property dealer shot dead inside Scorpio SUV:Wife receives chilling call after murder
stories.summary: In Meerut, a 23-year-old property dealer was murdered inside his Scorpio. On Monday night, attackers shot him twice and called his wife saying - "We've killed your husband, come and take the dead body." The incident occurred when he had left home to deliver food to someone. Shortly after, he called his wife saying - "Bittu alias Arvind Tyagi has kidnapped me. These people will kill me." After that, his phone was switched off. Family members informed the police and started searching for the property dealer. Late at night, the property dealer was found soaked in blood on the driver's seat inside the Scorpio. His head was on the car's steering wheel. One bullet had hit his forehead and another bullet had hit his neck. Family members took the property dealer to NCR Medical College, where doctors declared him dead. Property dealer Tushar Tyagi's 24th birthday was 2 days away. Tushar Tyagi was a resident of Hapur. He had married Shikha Tyagi two years ago. The couple has two children. The incident is from the Kharkhoda police station area. See 2 pictures- Read the entire incident in chronological order Tushar Tyagi, a resident of Doyami village in Hapur, was a farmer. He also worked in property dealing. Sister Mona said that on Monday evening around 8 pm, my brother received a phone call from someone. The caller said that I am hungry, get food prepared from home and bring it. My brother left home with food in a Scorpio. Around 9 pm at night, brother called sister-in-law Shikha. He said - Bittu alias Arvind Tyagi and his associates have kidnapped me and are taking me towards the jungle. These people will kill me. After this, my brother's phone got switched off. We all went out to search for brother. A village boy named Krish was also with us. We searched for him in all the nearby jungles, but brother was not found. Around 10 pm at night, we returned home. Just then Krish received a phone call. The caller said - I am Arvind alias Bittu Tyagi speaking, let me talk to Shikha. The caller Arvind told my sister-in-law that I have shot Tushar. His dead body is lying in the car, go and pick it up. After that he disconnected the phone. We informed the police. Along with the police, we reached near Panchi underpass on Hapur road. Here, inside the Scorpio, brother was found lying soaked in blood. Police and forensic team collected evidence from the spot and sent the body for post-mortem. Wife said - Tarun from the village had threatened to kill Wife Shikha Tyagi said that the accused Arvind alias Bittu Tyagi, a resident of Hapur, is the district president of Rashtriya Nav Nirman Dal. A few days ago, Tushar had a fight with Tarun Tyagi from the same village. During this, Tarun Tyagi had threatened to kill Tushar. Then Bittu Tyagi called both parties to his residence and got them to reconcile. I have filed a complaint against three people. Congress said- Criminals are on a rampage in Yogi Raj A post has been made from UP Congress's X (formerly Twitter) regarding the murder of Tushar Tyagi. The post states - In Meerut, 24-year-old Tushar Tyagi was shot dead after being kidnapped. After leaving home at night, his wife first received a call about his abduction, and shortly after, Tushar's body was recovered from a car parked under a bridge near the village. Under Yogi Adityanath's rule, criminals are running rampant. Please answer when the public will get relief from this goonda raj! SP Rural says - 4 teams deployed to catch the accused SP Rural Abhijit Singh informed that a case has been registered against three people based on the wife's complaint. Police have taken two people into custody for questioning. Four teams have been deployed to apprehend the accused.

stories.title: Virat Kohli, Anushka meet Premanand Maharaj after RCB's IPL win:Couple walked bare foot into the Ashram, third visit to Vrindavan in 2026
stories.summary: Indian cricketer Virat Kohli and his wife, Anushka Sharma, visited Vrindavan on Tuesday to seek the blessings of spiritual leader Premanand Maharaj. The couple arrived at the Kelly Kunj Ashram early in the morning and walked barefoot from their car into the premises before meeting the revered saint and receiving his blessings. The duo reportedly reached Vrindavan at around 7 AM, where they were welcomed by Premanand Maharaj’s disciples. Wearing face masks, Virat and Anushka headed straight into the ashram and spent nearly two hours there. When they emerged, Kohli was seen with sandalwood paste and a traditional tripundra mark on his forehead. Several videos and photographs of their visit later surfaced on social media. Earlier, on 20 April, coinciding with the occasion of Akshaya Tritiya, the couple had also visited Premanand Maharaj’s ashram, where they attended a satsang and sought his blessings. Their repeated visits reflect their continued spiritual association with the saint and his teachings. Virat, Anushka met Premanand Maharaj third time this year Earlier on Sunday, Royal Challengers Bengaluru defeated Gujarat Titans in the IPL 2026 title clash. After winning two consecutive titles with RCB, Kohli and his wife Anushka came to seek blessings from Premanand Maharaj for their third visit to the ashram this year. 5 images of Virat and Anushka's latest visit Virat Kohli replies ‘Radhe Radhe’ to cameraman One of the cameramen shooting Virat and Anushka's video said ‘Radhe Radhe’ to Virat, and he replied with ‘Radhe Radhe’. RCB won second IPL title two days back Just two days before his latest visit, Virat Kohli played a pivotal role in guiding Royal Challengers Bengaluru to their second consecutive IPL title. On May 31, RCB defeated Gujarat Titans by five wickets in the final at Narendra Modi Stadium to successfully defend their crown. Kohli starred on the biggest stage, smashing the fastest half-century of his IPL career in the summit clash. His match-winning knock earned him the Player of the Match award, capping off a memorable performance as RCB secured another historic championship triumph. Virat and Anushka’s seventh visit to Premanand Maharaj Virat Kohli and Anushka Sharma recently paid their seventh visit to spiritual leader Premanand Maharaj. The couple first met him on 4 January 2023, and have continued to visit his ashram regularly. Over the past three years, this marks their seventh meeting and their third visit in 2026. Earlier in 2025, they visited thrice in a year.

stories.title: Dasheri mango’s origin traced to fakir’s single seed from Afghanistan:Malihabad orchards of Lucknow grew from one tree
stories.summary: About 22 km from Lucknow on the Hardoi Highway is the town of Kakori. Here is the Gram Panchayat 'Dasheri'. The villagers claim that this is the world's oldest Dasheri mango tree, which is about 300 years old. The villagers say that a fakir from Afghanistan came to Malihabad with a seed and planted the first Dasheri mango tree there. Today, mango cultivation has expanded to cover 46,000 bighas. When the Dainik Bhaskar team reached ground zero to learn about the condition of this historical heritage, many interesting stories emerged. Read the report The fakir first ate it himself, and after liking it, had trees planted in Malihabad About 200 years ago, Fakir Mohammad Khan alias Goya fled from the Kandahar region of Afghanistan and reached Tonk in Rajasthan. With him was a community of Afridi Pathans. Seeing Goya's physique and his way of handling weapons, the Nawab of Tonk inducted him into his army. One day, the Nawab of Faizabad, Shuja-ud-Daula, came to Tonk. There he saw Goya's swordsmanship and horse riding. Pleased with this, he said to the Nawab of Tonk, 'Give me this Pathan.' Shuja-ud-Daula was so impressed with Goya that he made him the Commander-in-Chief of his army. Not only this, he entrusted Goya with the responsibility of protecting towns like Malihabad and Mohan. After this, the Pathans started settling in Malihabad. They built houses here. This was the era when there were no mango orchards in Malihabad. Goya also carried out basic development of these towns while living there. One day, he was going to Malihabad via Kakori on the Lucknow route. To rest from fatigue on the way, he sat under a huge mango tree in Kakori. This tree was laden with Dasheri mangoes. Seeing them, Purushottam, the owner of that tree, also reached there. He plucked mangoes and fed them to Goya. Goya was so pleased after eating the fruit that he decided to plant similar trees in Malihabad as well. This was the same Dasheri mango tree of Kakori, which people today call the 'Mother Tree' of Dasheri. Goya sought permission from the Nawab to plant Dasheri mango orchards here. Shuja-ud-Daula agreed. After this, mango cultivation began in Malihabad and Fakir Mohammad alias Goya became the first person to grow Malihabad mangoes. Today this tree is spread over 2 thousand square feet The oldest Dasheri mango tree appears special in 2 ways. 1. Less height, but more spread. Its branches are spread over an area of about 2,000 square feet. Its trunk is so wide that even three people cannot completely encircle it with outstretched arms. Just 5 feet above the ground, its 10 massive branches spread out in all directions. 2. No other large tree within this tree's radius. In the orchard where this tree was planted, there was no other mango tree as massive as this one in its vicinity. The whole village owns the tree, everyone takes care of it Seeing the tree, we headed towards the village. Here we met 55-year-old Bhagwandin. He explains, 'This tree has no owner, the entire village takes care of it. Someone gives water, someone fertilizer, and someone sprays medicine on this tree so that insects don't infest it. The result of this care is that this tree has survived for 300 years till now. It hasn't dried up. There's a tubewell nearby, from which it is irrigated.' Bhagwandin further says, 'Ever since I gained consciousness, I have seen this tree standing like this. There is no mango tree older than this here. However, this time the tree has fewer mangoes.' Village people said, 'People come from far and wide just to see the tree' Vinay Kumar from the village says, 'Leave us aside, even our fathers and grandfathers don't know how old this tree is. People say it's 300 years old, but I think it's more than 500 years old. People took the seeds of this very tree and planted Dasheri trees in Malihabad and across the country and world. That's why this tree is now called the "Mother Tree".' Meanwhile, Karan from the village says, 'Last year he tasted the mango from this tree for the first time. The taste was amazing and absolutely unique. Even today, people come from far and wide to see this tree. We are residents of this village, it feels good to see all this.' When it seemed the tree wouldn't survive It had dried up 4 years ago, became green again with great difficulty This Dasheri tree is still alive today. Behind it is the dedication and hard work of three generations of a family. Vikas Yadav, who takes care of it, says, 'I look after the tree, before me my father did, and before him my grandfather used to take care of it. Actually, the entire village helps in this work.' Vikas says, 'Four years ago, there came a time when all the leaves of the tree dried up and fell. Then it seemed that the tree would not survive, but we did not give up. We watered the roots, applied cow dung manure, and took great care. Within a few days, the tree became green and lush again. However, being a very old tree, its mangoes are not very large now, but the sweetness is still unmatched.' Village saved from becoming a dumping area because of the tree Projects received for the village considering it a 'heritage' during Akhilesh government We asked Vikas, has the village ever received any benefit because of this tree? He explains, 'It was in 2012. When Akhilesh Yadav became Chief Minister, schemes worth 14 crore rupees were received for the village in honor of this heritage. A lot of work was done with that money. However, the entire amount could not be spent, so many things remained incomplete.' Vikas says, ‘There was a plan to make this village a garbage dumping zone. People became worried about this. If garbage had started being dumped here, it would have become difficult to live in the village. The villagers protested against it, but it had no effect on the administration. Then this Dasheri tree was brought forward. It was said that the oldest Dasheri tree would be destroyed. Only then was the garbage dumping project shifted from here to Pankhedra, 10 kilometers away.’

stories.title: CEC Gyanesh Kumar offers prayers at Kailash Mahadev Temple:Visits with family after successful elections in 5 states
stories.summary: Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar arrived in Agra and visited Kailash Mahadev Temple early Tuesday morning with his wife Anuradha and his parents. At around 6:30 AM, he offered prayers, performed the aarti while holding his father's hand, and conducted a Dugdhabhishek ritual. He spent nearly 45 minutes at the temple. Speaking to reporters outside the temple, Kumar said that after the successful completion of elections in five states — West Bengal, Assam, Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Puducherry — he had come to Agra with his wife to seek blessings. He added that he first took the blessings of his parents before worshipping Lord Shiva. The Chief Election Commissioner said that upcoming elections would also be conducted in a transparent manner. Emphasizing the importance of a clean electoral roll, he urged citizens to obtain their voter ID cards and actively participate in the democratic process by casting their votes. Following his visit to Kailash Mahadev Temple, Kumar is scheduled to offer prayers at Mankameshwar Mahadev Temple. See 2 pictures... Touched parents' feet to seek blessings, also visited son-in-law's house The Chief Election Commissioner arrived in Agra from Delhi on Monday evening at 5:30 PM. He first reached his ancestral residence located in Vijay Nagar. He touched the feet of his father Dr. Subodh Kumar and mother Satyavati and sought their blessings. During this time, he also met with some people. Father Dr. Subodh Kumar Gupta has served as Chief Medical Officer. After meeting his parents, the Chief Election Commissioner reached the DM residence. Here he met his son-in-law and Agra DM Manish Bansal. His daughter Medha Roopam is the DM of Noida.

stories.title: Businessman's wife murdered by slitting throat in Saharanpur:Both ears cut off; blood-soaked body found lying on bed
stories.summary: In Saharanpur on Monday, a businessman's wife was murdered by slitting her throat. Both her ears were also cut off. The woman's blood-soaked body was found lying on the bed. Police have sent the body for post-mortem. The incident occurred in Ambehta town under Nakud police station. The deceased was identified as Poonam Mittal (60). Her husband Sanjay Mittal has a spare parts shop in Ambehta main market. Sanjay received a call on his phone from his wife's mobile around 4:08 PM in the evening. He said hello-hello several times, but there was no response from the other side. Sensing something wrong, he reached home taking a doctor along with him. See 3 pictures... Now the news in detail Sanjay Mittal said- When I reached home around 4:10 pm, I saw that the main door was open. In the room, my wife Poonam Mittal was lying on the floor drenched in blood. She had been attacked on the neck with a sharp weapon. It appears that my wife's throat was slit with a sharp weapon. Both her ears have also been cut off. The earrings she was wearing are missing. The cupboard kept in the room was also found open. In the drawing room, sweets on a plate and 2 glasses of water were also found. It is suspected that someone known has committed the crime. My son Vaibhav Mittal lives in Muzaffarnagar with his wife and children. He has a spare parts manufacturing factory and furniture showroom there. Police are examining CCTV footage from the vicinity. People's anger erupted against the police About an hour after receiving the information, Nakud police station in-charge Inspector Devesh Kumar Sharma reached the spot with police force and started the investigation. The anger of people present at the spot flared up over the police arriving late. Local people expressed their displeasure by questioning the working style of the chowki in-charge. Traders angered by the incident shut down the market. They also warned the police to solve the case soon. On receiving the information, Nakud Chairman Shiv Kumar Gupta, Ambehta Chairman Advocate Naeem Malik, and former Chairman Raj Kumar Khurana are also present at the spot.

stories.title: Father-daughter bond inked forever:Padmaja gets Prateek Yadav's portrait tattooed on her hand
stories.summary: Padmaja, the younger daughter of SP chief Akhilesh Yadav's brother Prateek Yadav, has paid an emotional tribute to her late father by getting his portrait tattooed on her hand. The tattoo features a touching image of Padmaja hugging her father, while Prateek is seen holding his daughter affectionately close to his chest. Tattoo artist Sakshi Panwar shared a video of the artwork on Instagram. In the caption, she wrote, “She said, ‘Will you please make a photo of Papa on my hand?’” Prateek Yadav passed away on May 13 in Lucknow. His wife, Aparna Yadav, is a BJP leader. The couple has two daughters, Prathama and Padmaja. The emotional tattoo has drawn attention on social media as a heartfelt remembrance of a father's bond with his daughter. Click on the photo above to watch the video.

stories.title: Lawyer’s murder shook Rajasthan, mystery remained unsolved for 14 yrs:Shooter enters office, fires two shots, escapes|Part-1
stories.summary: January 6, 2007 — a quiet evening in Pratapgarh. The city was carrying on as usual. Markets were bustling, shopkeepers were serving tea to customers, and life moved at its familiar pace in the Kotwali area. Then, at around 6:45 PM, a shocking incident shattered the calm and sent shockwaves across Pratapgarh. Inside his office in the Kotwali area, advocate Giriraj Joshi was seated with Vishal Salvi, Rahul Kabadi, and Narendra Kabadi. A chilly breeze drifted through the evening air as the group was engaged in what appeared to be an important discussion. Suddenly, the office door opened. A young man walked in. He appeared calm and showed no sign of hesitation. Without saying much, he moved directly toward Giriraj Joshi. Before anyone present could grasp what was happening, the man pulled out a firearm and opened fire. The first bullet struck Joshi near the right rib. A second shot hit his temple. The sound of gunfire echoed through the office. Giriraj Joshi collapsed from his chair and died on the spot. For a few moments, those present were frozen in shock, struggling to comprehend what had just unfolded. The assailant immediately fled the office. Outside, an accomplice was waiting on a motorcycle with the engine running. The two sped away toward the Mandsaur Road area. Within minutes, news of the killing spread across the city: Advocate Giriraj Joshi had been shot dead. Chaos on the streets Chaos erupted on the streets of Pratapgarh. Kotwali police reached the spot. Blood was splattered inside the office. Chairs were scattered. A crowd had gathered. Police cordoned off the area and registered a murder case against the attackers. But the real question was, why was Giriraj Joshi killed? Initially, the police thought it could be professional enmity. Giriraj Joshi was a well-known lawyer in the city. He had argued several major cases. As the investigation progressed, the case became more complicated. The murder was carried out with complete planning. The shooter reached directly to the office. He knew where Giriraj Joshi sat, at what time he would be alone, and which route to escape after the attack. This meant someone was keeping an eye on his every activity. He was playing an active role in a land dispute The police got their first major lead in the investigation when some people revealed that for the past several months, Giriraj Joshi had been very active in a land dispute. A series of meetings and negotiations was ongoing regarding approximately 10 bighas of land located near a religious site in the city. Why was this land so special? Discussions began that the land was adjacent to the religious site, and its value was continuously increasing. Many people wanted to buy it. Giriraj Joshi was playing a key role in the documents, lawsuits, and negotiations related to this land. The question before the police was: could someone commit murder over land? Meanwhile, different stories began spreading in the city. Some said - Giriraj knew too much, some whispered - there were crores at stake in the settlement... while others claimed - his murder had been decided long ago... Police combed through mobile call records Police combed through mobile call records. Questioned people. Deployed informers... but no clue about the shooter was found. There was definitely a whiff of conspiracy behind the murder, but the face wasn't coming forward. Meanwhile, police learned that a few days before the murder, there had been a series of meetings of several suspicious people. Among them were some local faces, as well as some outsiders. But there was no direct evidence against anyone. Then, suddenly, the investigation took a turn. Police started taking some suspects into custody one by one. The first name that came up was Bhauddin alias Bauddin. After that, Wasim Khan, Amin Khan, Shakir Bohra, Chunnu alias Imran, Mustafa...and then many other names came under the investigation's purview. The city was shocked. How could so many people be involved in one murder? Was this just a murder...or part of a bigger conspiracy? Police suspected that this was not an ordinary shootout, but a 'contract murder' carried out with complete planning. The most shocking thing was that the people whose names were coming up were connected to each other in different ways. Someone was in a land deal...someone had participated in settlement meetings...someone was allegedly in money transactions...and there were also some people whose names left people stunned. As the investigation progressed, police found out that several attempts at settlement had been made before the murder. In one meeting, there was also talk of giving ₹25 lakh and one bigha of land. After that, everything suddenly went wrong. Family's allegation - Attempt being made to suppress the truth What exactly happened that the conversation escalated from the table to bullets? This was the biggest question before the police. On the other hand, Giriraj Joshi's family alleged that very big people were behind the murder, and an attempt was being made to suppress the truth. The case also started taking on a political and social turn. Protests took place in Pratapgarh. Lawyers staged demonstrations. Pressure on the police kept increasing. But the real story was still in the dark. Because were the people who were visible in front...were they the real players? Or was there someone else behind the curtain...who was orchestrating this entire conspiracy? Trial transferred to another district During the investigation, police collected around 183 documents. Statements of 102 witnesses were recorded. The case had become so complicated that, finally, on the High Court's orders, the trial had to be transferred from Pratapgarh to Chittorgarh District and Sessions Court. 8 people were found guilty Time passed. Year after year, the hearing continued. Some accused died, and some remained in jail...but the truth of Giriraj Joshi's murder was still trapped in the court files. After 14 years...on October 1, 2021, the court pronounced its verdict. 8 people were found guilty. On what basis did the court find them guilty? Who was the mastermind? And why was such a dangerous conspiracy hatched for a piece of land?

stories.title: 'Won't Surya return?' Ailing brother keeps asking:Ghaziabad market shut for 5 days; people demand bulldozer action on Asad's house
stories.summary: Even five days after the murder of Surya Chauhan in Ghaziabad, Khoda market remains shut. Surya’s ailing elder brother, Yash Chauhan, keeps asking the same question: “Won’t Surya come back?” Moments later, he answers it himself in a subdued voice — “Surya is gone...” Grief and anger continue to grip the area, and an eerie silence prevails across Khoda on the fifth day after the killing. Following Surya’s death in a knife attack on Bakrid, many Muslim traders have kept their shops closed out of fear, while Hindu traders say securing justice for Surya is more important than resuming business. Authorities have also demolished properties linked to the accused, including the house of main accused Asad, who was killed in a police encounter. “First Surya must get justice; business can wait,” is the sentiment echoed by many traders in the market. Read Dainik Bhaskar's ground report on conversations with traders and the situation there. See 2 pictures- Surya's mother's health deteriorates, 400 personnel deployed Actually, on the day of Bakrid (28 May), Asad and his companions stabbed Surya to death in Khoda. In the early hours of Sunday (31 May), the police killed Asad in an encounter. The police have arrested 3 accused including Asad's father Nawab on charges of conspiracy. The fifth accused is still absconding. Even after the 5th day today, silence prevails in Khoda. The police have put up barriers on the main road. Police and RRF are deployed here. Workers of Hindu organizations are reaching Surya Chauhan's house while raising slogans. Surya's mother Saroj's health has deteriorated. After her son's death, the mother keeps losing consciousness. On Monday, Surya's ashes were immersed in the Ganga in Haridwar. After this, Surya's picture was placed outside the house, where people coming and going paid tribute by offering flowers. For security reasons, 400 personnel including one company of RRF and police are deployed within a 1 km radius of Surya's house in Khoda. BJP leader says - All are equally guilty, everyone's houses should be demolished BJP leader Harendra Singh has known the victim's family for a long time. He said that like Asad, the absconding accused should also be encountered. In this murder case, whoever is involved, all their houses should be demolished. Everyone is equally guilty in killing Surya. The one who stabbed is as guilty as the one who held his hands and the one who held his legs. Everyone killed Surya with complete planning. All the murderers should get equal punishment. Landlord says- Yash fell ill after father's death Surya Chauhan's family lives in a rented house. Landlord Pawan said- We have known them for 15 years. This family has been living with us for five years. About one and a half years ago, Surya's father died due to illness. After that, Surya's elder brother Yash Chauhan's health started deteriorating. Yash Chauhan can have seizures at any time. His treatment is ongoing at GTB Hospital in Delhi. Surya's mother Saroj keeps saying repeatedly that the son who was successful is the one who has gone. Traders said - How to open shops, we need security Trader Gautam Singh said - The market has been closed for 4 days. We will keep it closed further. Such a big incident has happened, no one has the courage to open their shop. Muslim traders' shops are also closed. Our only demand is that everyone gets security in the market. The way Surya has been murdered, anyone can be killed in the middle of the road like this. Therefore, traders need security. Kumkum Mishra said - Bulldozers should run on all accused's houses Local Kumkum Mishra says that we have a readymade garments shop. No matter how much loss occurs due to the market closure, but first we want justice. First Surya should get justice. All the people who committed the murder should be encountered. Bulldozers should be run on the homes of all those who killed Surya. What happened throughout Monday, know in points

stories.title: Akhilesh shifts to survey model for ticket distribution:Ends recommendation culture; Congress seat share may be 70-75 seats
stories.summary: In UP, the Samajwadi Party is conducting a survey of potential candidates before the 2027 assembly elections. The strength of ticket aspirants on the ground is being assessed in 2 ways. Akhilesh Yadav himself is monitoring the survey. Party sources claim that this time priority will be given to surveys and feedback in ticket distribution. Recommendations will not work. SP will field only those faces who have a strong popular base in their area. Their image will be spotless and they will be winning candidates. Retired IAS Alok Ranjan is leading the survey team. He has suggested giving 70 to 75 seats to Congress in his report. Retired IAS helping SP SP has started working on its potential candidates for 403 assembly seats in UP. According to sources, retired IAS officer of UP government Alok Ranjan is handling the command. Under his leadership, an office has also been set up in Gomti Nagar, Lucknow. Here, a professor from the Economics department of a Lucknow university, 2 research scholars, and several support staff have almost completed work on potential faces. This team has prepared a report related to the selection of candidates. It contains the names of SP's potential candidates seat-wise. This report mentions questions such as: This report will be presented before the core committee of the SP organization. Only after this will it be decided who will be the SP candidate on which seat. SP may give 70-75 seats to Congress in case of alliance The team of retired IAS officers has suggested in their report that SP's performance was weak in about 71 seats in UP in the 2022 assembly elections. If SP forms an alliance with Congress, Congress may pressure to contest elections on more than 100 seats. Whereas SP's effort should be to give only 70 to 75 seats. However, there may be tussle over Muslim-dominated seats. For instance, in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, Congress party won in Saharanpur, and Congress party's candidate stood second in Amroha. In such a situation, Congress may demand these seats. Due to controversies over ticket distribution in the 2022 and 2024 elections, SP has decided to conduct a survey through a private agency this time. Know about the 2 elections held in UP 2022 Assembly Elections: Factionalism dominated candidate selection After the 2022 assembly election results, SP leaders admitted that there were mistakes in ticket distribution. Giving tickets immediately to leaders who came from BJP or other parties caused significant resentment among the party's old and loyal workers. Allegations were made that in distributing tickets, personal 'lobbying' by local district presidents and senior leaders was given preference over ground reality or surveys. In many places, winnable candidates were ignored on the basis of factionalism. The party's internal review revealed that many seats were lost by very narrow margins because the candidates were not popular enough at the local level. Their booth management was weak. 2024 Lok Sabha Elections: Party kept changing tickets repeatedly During the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, SP's ticket distribution remained in the headlines and controversies the most. On several important seats like Meerut, Moradabad, Badaun and Gautam Buddha Nagar, SP changed its candidates two to three times. In Moradabad, the ticket of sitting MP ST Hasan was cancelled and given to Ruchiveera at the last moment, which caused turmoil at the local level. In Badaun, first Dharmendra Yadav was given the ticket, then his ticket was cancelled and given to Shivpal Singh Yadav, and finally Shivpal's son Aditya Yadav contested from there. Due to this exchange of tickets, the factionalism within SP came out in the open. Public disputes also emerged with allies like Congress and Pallavi Patel of 'Apna Dal (Kamerawadi)' over seat sharing and candidate selection. Survey will make it easier for SP to select candidates According to senior journalist Siddharth Kalhans, BJP-Congress have been conducting such surveys for 15-16 years. Now SP is also conducting such an exercise. SP-BSP used to select candidates through traditional methods earlier, which involved taking feedback from local leaders of the district. SP had worked on this strategy in the 2022 elections, but did not succeed in most places. Actually, many times the feedback that comes from district leaders is based on prejudice. The survey report will clarify the situation, making it easier to select candidates. Siddharth Kalahans says, 'For Akhilesh Yadav, winning seats is not important. For him, the candidate's victory will be crucial. That means whoever has a higher chance of winning the election will get the ticket. For this, he can even cut the ticket of his close associates or prominent leaders.'

stories.title: Lizard found in BHU's Dalmia Hostel mess:Upset students allege veg non-veg food was being prepared in same oil, VC demands report
stories.summary: A surprising case of a dead lizard found in the mess food at Dalmia Hostel of Banaras Hindu University, has come to forth, in which Vice-Chancellor has demanded an explanation report. Besides this, the mess has been closed until further orders. Actually, on Wednesday around 12 noon, students were having food in the mess when a lizard was spotted in the non-veg curry, by which time about 25-30 students had already eaten. When this matter came to light, some students started vomiting. 6 students kept under doctors' observation Due to the possibility of deteriorating health, Warden Prof. Raghav Mishra called an ambulance and sent six students to Sir Sunderlal Hospital, where they were given medicine and kept under doctors' observation. Meanwhile, on students' demand, the mess and canteen of Dalmia Hostel have been closed for now. Protesting by submitting a memorandum to the Warden, students said that the mess operator is also running the canteen, due to which the quality of food is not at all good. Was cooking veg and non-veg food in the same oil Students said - Veg and non-veg are cooked in the same oil. Utensils are also not cleaned properly. Toilets in the hostel are not cleaned on time. Students also listed several problems with drinking water. The warden told the students that there is no problem with the water cooler, but a water cooler kept downstairs was broken by a student who kicked it, after which it was placed inside the mess. Along with this, assurance was given to resolve other problems soon. Mess to remain closed with immediate effect until further orders The warden said - All students have been assured that in case of any health-related problem or other issue, they should immediately contact the hostel administration. The hostel administration will remain fully committed to the safety and health of the students. Considering the seriousness of the matter, in the presence of the administrative supervisor and all supervisors, a decision has been taken to close the concerned mess and canteen with immediate effect until further orders.

stories.title: BJP appoints 5 new district presidents in UP:Ram Sakal Patel gets Varanasi; Ramesh Gupta takes charge in Gorakhpur
stories.summary: BJP in UP announced 5 new district presidents on Thursday. State President Pankaj Chaudhary has assigned responsibilities to leaders from Awadh, Kashi and Gorakhpur regions. Those who received responsibilities Dilip Dev Patel from Ambedkar Nagar Ram Sakal Patel from Varanasi Kashinath Singh from Chandauli Ramesh Prasad Gupta from Gorakhpur Mahanagar Kali Prasad has been made district president of Deoria See the list In Chandauli, the home district of BJP organizational election in-charge and former Union minister Mahendra Nath Pandey, his rival Kashi Nath Singh has once again managed to become district president. The influence of state BJP chief Pankaj Chaudhary was visible in the party’s fourth list of district presidents. Out of the five newly appointed district chiefs, Dilip Dev Patel and Ram Sakal Patel belong to the Kurmi community. With this, the BJP has completed the appointment of district presidents in all 98 organisational districts ahead of the announcement of state-level office-bearers, formally concluding the organisational election process. Kali Prasad had earlier served as MLA from the reserved Salempur seat in Deoria. In the last election, his ticket was cut and Vijay Lakshmi Gautam, who had joined BJP from the Samajwadi Party, was made the candidate instead. Outgoing Deoria district president Bhupendra Singh had been facing significant opposition, with local workers and public representatives reportedly unhappy with his functioning. As a result, the party replaced him with Kali Prasad as the new district president.

stories.title: UP trader found dead in Chhatarpur home:Wife making rotis nearby as blood flows from nose, police break door open
stories.summary: In Chhatarpur district of Madhya Pradesh, a stock market trader died under suspicious circumstances. The body was found in a locked room of the house. The body was lying on a bed spread on the floor. Blood was flowing from the nose. A laptop was in a switched-on state in the room, with MCX and stock market related websites open on it. According to Sub Inspector Deepak Yadav of Orchha Road police station, the deceased has been identified as Rajesh Agarwal. The family originally hails from Baruasagar in Jhansi district of Uttar Pradesh. The family had sold their house there. He had been living in Chhatarpur for a long time. The family had shifted to a new house just about a month ago. Earlier they used to live in the house opposite. Rajesh had been locked in one room of the house for the past two days. He had not come out. Police reached the spot after receiving information. See these pictures... Rajesh Agrawal found dead on bedding spread on the floor The police knocked on the door for a long time, but there was no response from inside. After that, the door was pushed open. The police were also shocked to see the scene inside. Rajesh Agarwal was lying dead on a bed spread on the floor. He was wearing only a vest and underwear. MCX and stock market sites were open on the laptop According to the police, the room's light was on. A mobile phone was lying near the body, while a laptop was kept in front in an on state. The laptop screen had an MCX and stock market-related portal open, which was continuously showing figures. The police have secured electronic devices and other necessary evidence from the spot. The initial investigation has also revealed that the deceased was involved in share trading and MCX trading. Rajesh had been locked in the room for 2 days The deceased's 90-year-old mother told the police that Rajesh Agarwal had been locked in his room for the past two days. He had gone into the room on Tuesday night around 8 to 9 PM, after which he did not come out. Rajesh often used to stay locked in his room for several hours. In between, he would come out, eat a little food or take water from the fridge and go back to his room. This is why initially no one suspected much. Wife kept making rotis in the kitchen, son had no idea The police investigation also revealed that the deceased's wife and son are mentally unwell. Even when the police arrived at the scene, both were unable to comprehend the normal situation. The wife kept making rotis in the kitchen, while the son remained sitting on the house sofa. During this time, neither of them could understand what had happened inside the house. According to the police, only the deceased's elderly mother was in a condition to provide some information about the incident. No clear signs of struggle were found near the body, but blood was coming out from the deceased's nose. Son gave register with relatives' numbers During the investigation, the deceased's son gave the police a register in which mobile numbers of relatives and acquaintances were written. The police informed family members and community people based on that register. Not much contact with neighbors either Neighbors told the police that the family did not have much interaction with anyone. The household members were rarely seen outside. The initial information also reached the police through informants that Rajesh Agarwal had not been contactable for the past two days. Rumors of involvement in MCX trading and betting It is being reported that Rajesh Agarwal was involved in MCX trading and betting business. There are also rumors that he had been caught gambling before. However, the police have not officially confirmed this matter yet. The deceased's work, mobile data, laptop records, and financial activities will also be investigated. Awaiting FSL investigation and postmortem report After receiving information about the incident, the police called the FSL team to the spot. The team thoroughly examined the room and surrounding area. Necessary samples and electronic evidence have been collected from the scene. The real cause of death can only be revealed after the postmortem report and FSL investigation report arrive. Currently, the case is being investigated from every angle.

stories.title: UP education dept orders teachers to arrange 100 quintals fodder:Bareilly teachers say, tomorrow they’ll ask us to collect cow dung too
stories.summary: Teachers in Uttar Pradesh’s Bareilly district have expressed anger over a new directive issued by the Basic Education Department, asking them to arrange fodder for stray cattle while they are already engaged in census work. Under the order, each school has been assigned the responsibility of collecting 46 kg of fodder, while each block has been given a target of 100 quintals. The fodder is to be deposited at the offices of the Block Development Officer (BDO) or the Veterinary Officer. Warning of strict action for negligence Citing the District Magistrate’s order, the Basic Shiksha Adhikari (BSA) directed all Block Education Officers (BEOs) to ensure compliance. The letter stated that strict departmental action would be taken against schools and teachers found violating the directive. However, District Magistrate Avinash Singh later said he was not aware of the specific order, though he added that the administration was making efforts at every level for cow protection. Teachers have strongly objected to the directive, saying they are already burdened with excessive work. One teacher said- Teachers are already under stress because of excessive workload. Now such impractical orders from above are causing even more distress. Today we are being pressured to arrange fodder, tomorrow they may ask us to collect cow dung. Read the order issued by the Nawabganj Block Education Officer Teachers asked to submit purchase receipts After the Basic Education Department issued the order, BEOs in Nawabganj, Bhojipura, and Bhuta issued instructions at their respective levels. A letter issued on May 22 by the Block Education Officer of Nawabganj has since gone viral on social media. Copies of the order were also sent to the BSA and Veterinary Officer. Teachers were instructed to arrange fodder at their own level and deposit it at designated offices. The department also made it mandatory for schools to submit receipts after depositing fodder so that targets could be monitored. The administration instructed that the work be completed within one week. DM says cow protection is government priority District Magistrate Avinash Singh said stray cattle in the state are being cared for at temporary and permanent cow shelters. He said continuous efforts were underway to shift cattle roaming in the open into shelters, while new shelters were also being constructed. The DM appealed to citizens to donate fodder according to their financial capacity. He said- Fodder banks have been established in every block so that cattle do not face fodder shortages when required. Pastures are being developed to ensure the availability of green fodder and hay in shelters. Arrangements have also been made to purchase green fodder from farmers. Appeal to officials to adopt cattle Avinash Singh also said that sick and ageing cattle were being cared for under the supervision of veterinarians and district-level teams. He appealed to government officials to voluntarily adopt one animal each so that better care and protection could be ensured. The administration also plans to involve NGOs and social organisations in the campaign and urged members of the public to participate. BEO says teachers were ignoring orders Nawabganj BEO Satyadev said teachers were initially not complying with the instructions, which led to stricter wording in the order. He clarified that the directive had come from BSA Dr Vineeta and not from him personally. Satyadev said- Not even one quintal of fodder had been received so far. Just as parents sometimes need to be scolded to send children to school, the order was issued in a similar manner. He later clarified that the order had since been revised and that fodder donation was voluntary, with no pressure or compulsion. Teacher organisations threaten protest Bhanu Pratap Singh, District President and State Vice-President of the United Teachers Association (UTA), strongly criticised the order. He said- The primary duty of teachers is teaching, not collecting fodder. If such impractical orders are not stopped, teacher organisations will be forced to protest. Today the pressure is to arrange fodder, tomorrow they may ask us to collect cow dung. UTA Media Head Satendra Pal Singh called the directive completely illegal. He said the department should first consider whether such work actually falls within the responsibilities of teachers, who are already occupied with several administrative duties. District Vice-President Ramesh Maurya said such orders were against the dignity of teachers and warned that statewide protests could be organised if such directives continued. District Treasurer Hemant Kumar added that teachers were already busy with important duties such as the census and were under severe workload pressure. He appealed to the administration not to burden teachers with additional impractical responsibilities. Teacher says order harms professional dignity Teacher Rakhi Gangwar said the order asking teachers to collect fodder donations was against the dignity of the profession. She said teachers were already carrying out important responsibilities such as census work, Booth Level Officer (BLO) duties, voter list preparation, vote counting, and election work. ‘In such circumstances, asking teachers to go door-to-door collecting fodder is completely inappropriate,’ she said. Rakhi Gangwar added that farmers themselves were struggling with fodder shortages and often had limited supplies even for their own livestock. She said teachers always follow necessary departmental instructions, but opposition to “wrong and unnecessary orders” would continue.

stories.title: Bashir Badr’s house was burnt during Meerut riots:He then wrote, 'Log tut jaate hain ek ghar banane mein, tum taras nahi khaate bastiyaan jalaane mein'
stories.summary: ‘Log tut jaate hain ek ghar banane mein, tum taras anhi khaate bastiyan jaalane mein’ These lines were spoken by renowned Urdu poet Bashir Badr after seeing his house burnt during the 1987 Meerut riots. Rioters had set his home on fire, an incident that deeply affected the celebrated ghazal writer. On returning to the city, he expressed his pain through poetry. Dr Bashir Badr passed away in Bhopal on Thursday at the age of 91. A significant part of his life remained closely connected to Uttar Pradesh. Though his ancestral roots were in Ayodhya, he was born in Kanpur. He later studied at Aligarh Muslim University and eventually became head of the Urdu department at Meerut College, where he served for 17 years. After the Meerut riots and the burning of his house, he permanently shifted to Bhopal. Born in Kanpur, father worked in police department Bashir Badr’s real name was Syed Muhammad Bashir. He was born on February 15, 1935, in Kanpur. His ancestral village was Mauja Bakia in Ayodhya district. His father, Syed Muhammad Nazir, worked in the police department. Bashir Badr studied up to Class 3 at Halim Muslim College in Kanpur before his father was transferred to Etawah. He later completed high school at Muhammad Siddique Islamia College in Etawah. However, after his father’s death, his education was interrupted as family responsibilities fell upon him. He joined the police department on a salary of Rs 85 per month. During this period, he married Qamar Jahan and had three children. Despite his job responsibilities, he remained deeply passionate about poetry from a young age. First Ghazal published in Class 7 Bashir Badr’s literary talent emerged early. While studying in Class 7, one of his ghazals was published in Niaz Fatehpuri’s magazine ‘Nigar’. The publication established his identity in Etawah’s literary circles. By the age of 20, his ghazals were regularly appearing in major magazines across India and Pakistan. He later decided to resume his education and earned BA, MA, and PhD degrees from Aligarh Muslim University. During his doctoral studies, his research supervisor was Professor Aal-e-Ahmad Suroor. His thesis focused on “A Critical Study of Urdu Ghazal After Independence.” After completing his BA in 1967, he resigned from the police service. He supported his family through university scholarships and earnings from mushairas. After receiving his PhD in 1974, he briefly taught at Aligarh Muslim University. See pictures of Bashir Badr related to Meerut First wife’s last rites performed by neighbours Bashir Badr was later appointed at Meerut College and settled in Vikas Colony in Meerut’s Shastri Nagar area. In May 1984, while he was in Pakistan attending a mushaira, his wife passed away. In his absence, neighbours performed her last rites. In 1986, he married Dr Rahat Sultan of Bhopal. Meerut riots changed his life Communal riots broke out in Meerut in April 1987 and continued for nearly three months. More than 100 people were reportedly killed during the violence. As tensions escalated, Bashir Badr went to stay with relatives, while his younger son Binu remained at home. On the day of the attack, a mob reportedly entered the colony from its southern side early in the morning. Since it was morning, most residents were indoors. At the time, Binu was in a nearby park outside the house. The mob attacked Bashir Badr’s house, vandalised it extensively, and later set it on fire. Residents of the colony eventually gathered and intervened. Bashir Badr also confronted the rioters in an attempt to save his home. Although the family later returned after the situation stabilised, the incident left a deep emotional impact on him. The family remained in Meerut for another year before selling the house in 1988 and relocating permanently to Bhopal. Poetry written after his house was burnt After the destruction of his house, Bashir Badr expressed his grief through poetry. He wrote- Bade shauq se mera ghar jala, koi aanch tujhpe na aaegi, Yeh jubaan kisi ne khareed li, yeh kalam kisi ka gulaam hai.Bekhabar kursiyaan aankh malti rahin, bastiyan begunahon ki jalti rahin.Kisne jalai bastiyaan bazaar kyun lutte, Mein chaand par gaya tha, mujhe kuch pata nahi.

stories.title: 'I kept screaming in pain all night, nobody came':ITBP Jawan’s mother alleges medical negligence after hand amputation in Kanpur
stories.summary: "I was admitted to the ICU of Krishna Hospital on May 13. Medicines were being administered through an IV drip when I suddenly felt severe pain in my hand. I kept screaming in pain. A staff member came, tightly wrapped my hand with white tape and said everything would be fine shortly before leaving", these statements were given to police by Nirmala Devi, the mother of an ITBP commando posted in Kanpur. She alleged that instead of reducing, the pain kept increasing through the night. Despite repeatedly crying for help, no one attended to her. By the next morning, her hand had turned black. “When my son Vikas reached the hospital the next day, he saw the condition of my hand and immediately shifted me to Paras Hospital. Doctors there said the hand had to be amputated. Had my complaints been taken seriously in time, my hand could probably have been saved,” she told police. ITBP Jawan accuses hospitals of negligence The incident involves ITBP commando Vikas Singh, whose mother Nirmala Devi was admitted to Krishna Super Speciality Hospital near Tatmil Crossing in Kanpur for treatment related to stomach and breathing issues. The family has alleged that negligence during treatment caused a severe infection in her hand, ultimately leading to amputation. Angered by the incident, Vikas Singh reached the Police Commissioner’s office on May 19 carrying his mother’s amputated hand and demanded strict action against Krishna Hospital. Police Commissioner Raghubir Lal referred the matter to the Chief Medical Officer (CMO) for investigation. An initial inquiry report reportedly failed to establish clear responsibility, triggering outrage among ITBP personnel. On May 24, around 50 ITBP personnel, along with senior officers, reached the Police Commissioner’s office demanding action. Following the protest, the CMO ordered a fresh investigation. The second inquiry reportedly found negligence on the part of both hospitals, after which police registered a case and began investigation. “Nobody came to check on me” In her statement, Nirmala Devi said she had been experiencing breathing difficulties, after which her son admitted her to Krishna Hospital. Doctors shifted her to the ICU and inserted a cannula for intravenous medication. “Soon after medicines were administered, my hand began hurting badly. I started crying and screaming. A staff member came, pulled my hand tightly, wrapped white tape around it and left saying the pain would stop,” she said. However, the pain continued worsening throughout the night. “I kept crying and screaming in pain, but nobody came to check on me. By morning, my hand had turned black,” she alleged. Family claims delay in treatment worsened infection According to Nirmala Devi, when her son arrived the next morning, she informed him about the unbearable pain. The IV line was removed, but her condition did not improve. She was later shifted to Paras Hospital on Bithoor Road. Doctors there eventually amputated her hand after the infection reportedly spread severely. She told police that timely medical attention and immediate removal of the IV line could have prevented the amputation. See 3 pictures of the Police Commissionerate siege How the incident unfolded Vikas Singh, a resident of Khaga Hathgam in Fatehpur district, is currently posted with the 32nd Battalion of the ITBP in Maharajpur, Kanpur. He said his 56-year-old mother had breathing problems, weakness and constipation. She was initially examined at the ITBP hospital in Maharajpur. On May 13, 2026, her condition deteriorated suddenly and doctors referred her to a higher medical centre empanelled with the ITBP. While transporting her in an ambulance, they got stuck in severe traffic congestion. Due to the worsening condition of his mother, Vikas admitted her to Krishna Hospital instead. He alleged that doctors administered a wrong injection, after which her hand turned black and swelling kept increasing. She was later shifted to Paras Hospital on May 14, but by then the infection had spread significantly. Doctors amputated her hand on May 17. ITBP personnel protested outside Commissioner’s office Following the incident, Vikas Singh spent three days visiting police outposts, police stations and the Police Commissioner’s office seeking action against the hospitals. Police Commissioner Raghubir Lal later took cognisance of the matter after seeing the amputated hand and ordered an impartial investigation. On May 23, around 40 to 50 ITBP personnel reached the commissioner’s office demanding a fair probe. Following mounting pressure, authorities ordered another medical investigation. The fresh report submitted on May 25 reportedly found both hospitals guilty of negligence.

stories.title: 2 burnt alive after truck-dumper collision in Gorakhpur:Fire erupted on Lucknow highway, injured driver and helper escaped by jumping
stories.summary: A dumper driver and cleaner were charred to death after a truck and dumper collided and caught fire in Gorakhpur on Thursday morning. The truck driver and helper also suffered burn injuries but managed to save themselves by jumping out of the vehicle. The accident took place in the Ramgarhtal police station area on the Kushinagar-Lucknow highway. Following the incident, a traffic jam stretching nearly five kilometres formed on the highway. Five fire brigade vehicles reached the spot and brought the blaze under control after nearly an hour of firefighting efforts. The injured truck driver and helper were admitted to the district hospital for treatment. Police identified the dumper driver as Satyendra, son of Ramkomal, a resident of Dhamora village in Basti district. The cleaner, Shiva, was a resident of Fatehpur. See 4 pictures of the accident Dumper came from wrong side, collision triggered fire According to police, the truck loaded with maize was travelling from Kushinagar to Lucknow on the four-lane highway. Around 5 am on Thursday, a dumper carrying construction material allegedly entered the highway from the wrong side near Ajwania village. The vehicles collided head-on, causing the truck to overturn on the roadside and catch fire immediately. The flames quickly spread to the dumper. The dumper driver and cleaner became trapped inside the vehicle. Before they could be rescued, the fire intensified and both were burnt alive inside the cabin. The collision also crushed the front portion of the truck. Although the truck driver and helper sustained burn injuries, they managed to jump out and survive. Villagers alerted Police and Fire Department Local villagers rushed to the spot after the accident and informed the police. Police teams and five fire tenders reached the scene and controlled the fire after nearly two hours. The injured victims were shifted to hospital by ambulance. Only skeletal remains found inside dumper After the fire was extinguished, police teams found only skeletal remains inside the dumper. Officials collected the remains and initiated further legal procedures. Police said DNA testing would be conducted to formally identify both victims.

stories.title: Dog unleashed on electricity dept team during power theft raid:Five employees assaulted inside house in Lucknow
stories.summary: A team from the electricity department was allegedly attacked while investigating power theft in Lucknow. The attackers reportedly assaulted a junior engineer (JE) and staff members with kicks, punches and shovels, and even unleashed a German Shepherd dog on the JE. The injured officials somehow escaped from the spot. Five electricity department employees, including the JE, were hurt in the attack and later admitted to a hospital. The incident took place around 4 pm on Wednesday in Lucknow’s Jankipuram area. JE Ashok Kumar filed a complaint with the police. In a separate incident, another electricity inspection team was attacked by a mob in the Saadatganj area while attempting to stop power theft. See pictures Team allegedly trapped inside house and assaulted According to officials, the electricity department had been receiving complaints about power theft in Jankipuram for several days. On Wednesday evening, JE Ashok Kumar reached the area with a five-member team that included Radheshyam Yadav, Ayush Gaur, Shivam Yadav and Manish Kumar. Ashok Kumar said the team went to the house of consumer Ajay Dixit and asked to inspect the electricity meter. Initially, Dixit allegedly refused, but later took the team inside the house to show the meter. The JE alleged that several family members were already present inside the house. During the inspection, an argument broke out between the power department team and the family members. Soon after, the accused allegedly began assaulting the officials inside the house. The attackers reportedly hit the team with shovels and physically assaulted them with kicks and punches. JE says pet dog was unleashed on him The junior engineer alleged that Ajay Dixit released his pet German Shepherd dog during the attack. The dog allegedly bit and scratched him severely, leaving deep injuries on his body. The attackers also allegedly snatched his mobile phone. The team somehow managed to escape and informed the police. Police later arrived at the scene and shifted the injured employees to a hospital. Jankipuram Station House Officer Vinod Tiwari said a case has been registered against Ajay Dixit and four unidentified persons. Investigation is underway. Another attack on electricity team in Saadatganj In another incident, an electricity department team was attacked in the Tobacco Market area of Chowpatia in Saadatganj. SDO Jitendra Gurjar and JE Khursheed Anwar had gone there with their team for electricity checking operations. Officials alleged that as employees began removing illegal power connections from electric poles, Jalil Ahmad and Abdul Khaliq, along with a crowd of 30 to 40 unidentified people, attacked the team. The mob allegedly tore official documents and dragged contractual worker Santosh Yadav before assaulting him with kicks, punches and sharp weapons. Santosh suffered serious injuries to his face and body. Police have registered FIRs against named and unidentified attackers in both Saadatganj and Jankipuram police stations, and raids are being conducted to arrest the accused.

stories.title: UP’s senior-most IPS officer without posting for 2 years:Multiple top cops handling extra charges raises questions
stories.summary: Major responsibilities in the Uttar Pradesh Police department are currently concentrated among a few senior officers, while several others remain without significant assignments despite their seniority. The most prominent example is 1990-batch IPS officer Renuka Mishra, the senior-most IPS officer in Uttar Pradesh Police, who has reportedly remained without a formal responsibility for over two years. At the same time, acting DGP Rajeev Krishna, DG Alok Singh and ADG Amitabh Yash — known for leading anti-gangster operations — are handling multiple additional charges simultaneously. Senior officers without major responsibilities Senior-most IPS officer still without posting Renuka Mishra was removed from the Uttar Pradesh Police Recruitment and Promotion Board in February 2024 after the police constable recruitment exam paper leak controversy. After being kept on a waiting list for nearly three months, she was attached to the DGP office. Despite being senior to current acting DGP Rajeev Krishna, who belongs to the 1991 batch, she has reportedly remained without a significant assignment for more than two years. Antony Dev Kumar posted to “shunting post” The post of ADG Rules and Manual is also considered a sidelined assignment within the department. Senior officer Antony Dev Kumar is currently posted there, where officials say the workload is minimal. However, Kumar has had an accomplished career, including international service. He received the United Nations Interim Administration Mission in Kosovo (UNMIK) Medal in 2004-05. Jasveer Singh suspended for seven years 1992-batch IPS officer and ADG-rank official Jasveer Singh has remained suspended for seven years. He was suspended on February 14, 2019, over alleged violations of service rules. Although an inquiry was initiated, no final outcome has yet emerged. Navniet Sekera posted at training school ADG Navniet Sekera has been posted at the Police Training School in Unnao since March 2022. Officials point out that comparable training schools in Jalaun, Sultanpur and Moradabad are being headed by officers two to three ranks junior to him. Officers handling multiple additional charges Several senior officers are currently handling multiple departments simultaneously. DG B.K. Singh He is overseeing: Traditionally, Cyber Crime and UP-112 were handled separately by IG or ADG-rank officers. DG Alok Singh Apart from the Provincial Armed Constabulary (PAC), he is also handling the Special Security Force (SSF). DG D.K. Thakur In addition to Home Guards, he also holds charge of Civil Defence. Rajeev Sabbarwal Along with Training, he is also serving as Director of the Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar Police Academy. ADG Amitabh Yash He currently handles: A. Satish Ganesh Apart from Traffic, he also oversees Crime. Padmaja Chauhan She is handling both: Three officers considered closest to the Chief Minister Rajeev Krishna Acting DGP Rajeev Krishna is considered among Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath’s most trusted officers. When the BJP government came to power in Uttar Pradesh, Rajeev Krishna was serving as an ADG-rank officer on central deputation. After returning, he was posted at the Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar Police Academy in Moradabad. Soon afterward, he was given charge as ADG of Lucknow and later Agra Zone. Following his promotion to DG rank in 2024, he was assigned to the Vigilance Department — a charge he still holds. After the retirement of former DGP Prashant Kumar, Rajeev Krishna was appointed acting DGP. Alok Singh DG Alok Singh, currently heading the PAC, is also regarded as a trusted officer of the Chief Minister. After returning from central deputation, he was initially posted as IG of the PAC East Zone and later shifted to Kanpur Range. In July 2019, he became IG of Meerut Range and was later promoted to ADG rank. When the police commissionerate system was introduced in Uttar Pradesh, Alok Singh became the first Police Commissioner of Gautam Buddh Nagar. After nearly three years there, he was shifted to Kanpur Zone before eventually being promoted to DG rank and assigned PAC responsibilities. Amitabh Yash ADG Amitabh Yash is also counted among the Chief Minister’s trusted officers. In 2017, he was serving as IG Railway before being appointed head of the STF soon after the BJP government came to power. Even after his promotion to ADG rank in January 2020, he continued to lead STF, becoming the longest-serving STF chief in the state. In 2024, after Prashant Kumar became DGP, Amitabh Yash was additionally entrusted with maintaining law and order across the state. Experts raise questions over multiple charges Senior journalist Rajendra Kumar said assigning multiple departments to one officer affects efficiency. According to him, cybercrime has become a major challenge in Uttar Pradesh, and officers heading such important units may not be able to devote equal attention to additional responsibilities. He added that different departments operate from separate offices, meaning officers spend considerable time travelling between locations instead of focusing on administration. Rajendra Kumar also said that if the government believes one officer can efficiently handle two or three departments, the overall number of senior officers should be reduced to cut administrative expenses.

stories.title: Eid-ul-Adha celebrated under tight security across UP:Muslim community offers Namaz at Taj Mahal, drone surveillance in Kanpur
stories.summary: Eid-ul-Adha (Bakrid) was celebrated across Uttar Pradesh on Thursday with prayers being offered at mosques and Eidgahs under tight security arrangements. Special prayers were held inside the premises of the Taj Mahal in Agra, where even Nigerian tourists participated in the namaz and exchanged Eid greetings. Police personnel were deployed outside Eidgahs and mosques in Sambhal and Varanasi to maintain law and order during the celebrations. Drone surveillance in Kanpur, flag march in Saharanpur Authorities intensified security monitoring in several sensitive districts. In Kanpur, police used drones to monitor crowded areas and ensure peaceful celebrations. In Saharanpur, District Magistrate Arvind Chauhan and Senior Superintendent of Police Abhinandan conducted a flag march ahead of Eid prayers. Lalitpur SP offers money to poor after Namaz In Lalitpur, Superintendent of Police Mohammad Mushtaq distributed money to poor people standing outside after offering Eid prayers. Meanwhile, Samajwadi Party district vice-president Bhajan Lal Kushwaha showered flower petals on police personnel and worshippers as a gesture of harmony and celebration. Political leaders expected at Lucknow Eidgah Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak and Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav were expected to visit the Aishbagh Eidgah in Lucknow during the celebrations. Muslim clerics appeal for peaceful celebrations Muslim religious leaders appealed to people to offer prayers only inside mosques and Eidgah premises and avoid praying on roads. They also urged citizens to perform animal sacrifice only inside homes or designated slaughterhouses and not in open public places. Mayawati and Akhilesh extend Eid greetings Bahujan Samaj Party chief Mayawati and Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav extended greetings to people on the occasion of Eid-ul-Adha.

stories.title: 4 arrested for suspected links to Pak-based terror group:Accused planned blasts at BJP offices, hospitals and schools
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Anti-Terrorist Squad (ATS) and Special Task Force (STF) on Wednesday arrested four suspected terrorists allegedly linked to a Pakistan-backed terror module. According to investigators, the accused were planning blasts targeting BJP offices, hospitals, schools and several other sensitive locations across the state. Two of the accused are residents of Saharanpur, while the other two belong to Haridwar and Muzaffarnagar. All four were arrested from Saharanpur. Investigators claim the accused were in contact with Pakistani gangster Shahzad Bhatti and gangster Abid Jatt, allegedly acting on instructions from Pakistan’s intelligence agency ISI. Suspects allegedly received targets through Instagram During interrogation, accused Mehkab and Gagandeep alias Guri reportedly told investigators that they communicated with Shahzad Bhatti and Abid Jatt through Instagram. According to ATS officials, Abid Jatt instructed them to conduct reconnaissance of: The suspects allegedly planned to target these locations using explosives. Investigators said the accused were also told that more targets would be assigned after completing the first operation. stories.title: IMD issues rain alert for 69 districts in UP:Hailstorm warning in 24 districts, pre-monsoon activity expected after four days
stories.summary: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued an alert for thunderstorms and rainfall in 69 districts of Uttar Pradesh, while 24 districts are likely to witness hailstorms. Wind speeds may reach up to 100 kmph in 32 districts. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has predicted heavy rain accompanied by thunderstorms across the state between May 28 and May 31. On Wednesday, May 28, hailstorms are likely in 24 districts of western Uttar Pradesh. In eastern UP, strong winds are expected to blow at speeds of 60 to 70 kmph, with gusts possibly touching 80 kmph. Meteorologists say a new western disturbance is becoming active, which may lead to a temperature drop of 6 to 8 degrees Celsius. Banda hottest city in Uttar Pradesh Banda in the Bundelkhand region recorded the highest temperature in the state at 47.8°C. In Jhansi, water sprinklers were used on roads to reduce surface temperatures amid the severe heatwave. In Ayodhya, an auto-rickshaw caught fire while moving on the road. Passengers jumped out to save their lives. See 2 pictures- Moist winds from Bay of Bengal and Arabian Sea affecting weather Senior scientist Atul Kumar Singh from Lucknow said the weather is changing rapidly due to the activation of a new western disturbance and the influence of moisture-laden winds coming from the Bay of Bengal and the Arabian Sea. According to him, these systems are creating favorable conditions for widespread rainfall and strong thunderstorms across the state. The Meteorological Department estimates that temperatures could fall by 8 to 10 degrees Celsius because of rainfall and strong winds, bringing relief from heatwave conditions for nearly a week. Red alert issued for Western UP and Terai region The weather department has advised people in western Uttar Pradesh and the Terai region to remain especially cautious on May 29. A red alert has been issued in some areas where wind speeds may exceed 100 kmph. However, Bundelkhand and the Prayagraj region are expected to continue experiencing intense heat and heatwave conditions on Thursday. Weather forecast for the next four days Why is it raining despite no major monsoon system? Meteorologists explained that Uttar Pradesh has witnessed extremely high temperatures over the past few days, creating a sharp contrast between surface temperatures and upper atmospheric conditions. In addition: These combined systems have created favorable conditions for thunderstorms and rainfall across the state. Uttar Pradesh may receive below-normal monsoon rainfall The Meteorological Department has warned that Uttar Pradesh could receive below-normal rainfall during the upcoming southwest monsoon season between June and September. Director General of Meteorology Dr. M. Mohapatra said La Nina-like conditions in the Pacific Ocean are weakening, while signs of El Nino are emerging. This transition could weaken the southwest monsoon and reduce rainfall this year. He also noted that reduced snowfall in the Northern Hemisphere between January and March may affect monsoon patterns. UP received excess rainfall last year According to the Meteorological Department, Uttar Pradesh recorded average rainfall between 870 mm and 900 mm during the 2025 monsoon season from June to September. This was around 10 to 15 percent above the normal monsoon average. How to protect yourself from heatwave conditions Experts say avoiding direct sunlight alone is not enough during extreme summer conditions. Following proper precautions is equally important to prevent heatstroke and dehydration. Precautions before going outdoors Small mistakes before stepping out in intense heat can significantly increase the risk of heat-related illnesses. Sudden exposure to high temperatures and poor dietary habits may quickly lead to overheating and dehydration. Important heatwave safety measures During the nine-day “Nautapa” period, temperatures often rise between 40°C and 45°C. People still need to step outside for work and daily responsibilities, increasing the risk of: Health experts advise people to carry water, avoid direct sunlight during peak hours, wear light cotton clothing, and remain alert to symptoms of heat-related illness.
