stories.title: Agra ride accident claims teenager’s life, 5 blamed:Authorities earn crores annually but ignored bare minimum safety measures
stories.summary: A 16-year-old boy from Firozabad died after falling from a zipline ride at Chowpati Adventure Park in Agra. The teenager’s parents broke down while holding his body in their arms after the accident. Eyewitnesses alleged that neither first aid nor immediate emergency assistance was provided at the spot. Employees of the company operating the adventure activities also allegedly failed to help the injured boy in time. Following a complaint by the family, police registered a case against the owner, manager, and safety in-charge of adventure company Every Other Day Adventure Private Limited. The manager and safety in-charge have been sent to jail. However, no action has yet been taken against the company’s two directors, and no accountability has been fixed on officials of the Agra Development Authority (ADA). Here is a detailed look at the five parties whose alleged negligence may have contributed to the tragic accident. Know who are the 5 people responsible for Kunal's death, due to whom the terrible accident happened. Responsibilities of the safety in-charge The safety in-charge of the adventure company was expected to ensure that proper safety procedures were followed before the ride began. Key responsibilities included Essential safety gear that should have been provided According to the complaint, several critical safety measures were either inadequate or missing: Responsibilities of the adventure park manager The manager overseeing operations at Chowpati Adventure Park was responsible for ensuring compliance with operational and safety standards. The manager’s duties included: Responsibilities of the company directors The directors of Every Other Day Adventure Private Limited were responsible for supervising all adventure activities and ensuring overall safety compliance. Their key responsibilities included: The company operates adventure parks not only in Agra but also in Delhi and Ghaziabad. It had taken Chowpati Adventure Park in Agra on lease. As the operating agency, the company was responsible for providing high-quality safety equipment, hiring trained staff, and conducting periodic safety reviews. Questions raised over emergency preparedness Additional responsibilities of the directors The company directors were also expected to: After Kunal’s fall, no immediate first aid was reportedly available at the site. Critics argue that the directors should have ensured proper emergency medical arrangements at the adventure facility. What was the responsibility of the Agra Development Authority? The Agra Development Authority (ADA), which owns the property, is also facing questions over supervision and safety oversight. ADA’s responsibilities included: Although the adventure company was operating the facility under a contractual agreement, the property itself belongs to ADA. As the owner, ADA was responsible for monitoring safety compliance and ensuring that dangerous negligence was not taking place at the public venue. Officials are now facing criticism for alleged lapses in oversight. ADA Vice-Chairperson M. Arunmoli said a five-member committee has been formed to investigate the incident. The panel, led by ADA Secretary Sanjay Kumar, is expected to submit its report within a day or two. Company signed a 9-year agreement with ADA The adventure company began operations at Agra’s Chowpati in October 2025. The agreement with ADA was signed for nine years, with an option to extend the contract for another six years after review, allowing the company to operate the facility for up to 15 years. The annual contract value is reportedly around Rs 1.8 crore. About Agra’s Chowpati adventure park Chowpati was developed inside Zonal Park in Taj Nagari Phase-2, around 3 km from the eastern gate of the Taj Mahal. The park includes food courts offering dishes from Agra and other parts of India and was promoted as a family-friendly recreational destination for morning walks and evening outings. The facility was inaugurated in November 2023. Approximately 800 to 1,000 visitors come to the park daily, with around 400 to 600 youngsters participating in adventure rides every day. Adventure activities at the site include: The company charged Rs 400 per person for the zipline activity. Entry to Chowpati suspended after accident Following the tragedy, the Chowpati facility has been shut down. Since Monday morning, the main gate has remained locked from inside, and ticket counters have been closed. The usually crowded venue now appears deserted, with only a few employees seen inside the premises. Five-Member Committee Investigating the Incident After the accident, ADA Vice-Chairperson M. Arunmoli constituted a five-member inquiry committee led by ADA Secretary Sanjay Kumar. The panel includes: The committee is investigating: How the accident happened The victim, Kunal, was the 16-year-old son of Firozabad bangle trader Pankaj Agarwal. On May 24, while riding the zipline in front of his parents and brother, Kunal reportedly fell nearly 45 feet headfirst after the safety hook attached to his harness broke mid-ride. He struck the railing before crashing to the ground. According to witnesses, he died on the spot after writhing in pain. At the time of the incident, Kunal’s mother and brother were recording videos from below. The entire accident was captured on their mobile phone. The family had come to Agra from Firozabad for a leisure trip. His grieving father later said, My son died because of the negligence of the zipline operators. I had brought him here for an outing. How will I now take his body back home?

stories.title: Why AK Sharma failed to improve electricity supply in UP?:Rift with power corporation chief, bureaucratic experience didn’t help
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Energy Minister Dr. AK Sharma, a former Gujarat-cadre IAS officer who spent 32 years in bureaucracy, entered politics with high expectations. The BJP made him a Member of the Legislative Council (MLC) in UP and, within six months, appointed him as the party’s state vice-president. Currently, Sharma is serving as Urban Development and Energy Minister in the Yogi Adityanath government, he is facing mounting criticism as electricity supply has emerged as a major issue ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections. Public anger over power cuts has spilled onto the streets. BJP MPs and MLAs are writing directly to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath over the crisis. Meanwhile, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav has promised 300 units of free electricity if his party returns to power. The crisis became so serious that the Chief Minister himself intervened, suspending two engineers and issuing show-cause notices to two others. This has raised a larger question: Why has AK Sharma, who worked for 13 years in the Gujarat Chief Minister’s Office and six years in the Prime Minister’s Office, failed to deliver results in Uttar Pradesh’s energy department? Read the report… Uttar Pradesh has the highest power demand in India In May, Uttar Pradesh’s daily power requirement touched nearly 31,824 MW, making it the highest electricity-consuming state in the country. Maharashtra ranked second with 29,463 MW demand. The state receives electricity from five major sources: 1. State-owned thermal plants (7,500–8,500 MW) Plants such as Anpara, Obra, Harduaganj, and Parichha handle the state’s base power load round the clock. 2. Joint ventures and Private companies (7,000–9,000 MW) UP procures power through long-term agreements from joint projects like Meja and Ghatampur, as well as private plants in Lalitpur, Rosa, and Prayagraj. 3. Central government allocation (7,000–8,000 MW) The state receives its quota from central power plants such as Singrauli, Rihand, Unchahar, and Dadri. 4. Power banking and exchanges UP supplies excess winter electricity to hill states like Jammu Kashmir and Himachal Pradesh and receives it back during summer demand spikes. 5. Renewable and Hydro power Solar energy from Bundelkhand helps manage daytime air-conditioner loads, while hydroelectric projects at Rihand and Obra support evening peak demand. Why the crisis deepened: Three major reasons Minister vs Chairman: Internal conflict hurt the system According to Avadhesh Verma, chairman of the Consumers’ Council, relations between Energy Minister AK Sharma and Power Corporation Chairman Ashish Goyal have not been smooth. The minister reportedly opposed the removal of contractual workers, but the chairman ignored his objections and terminated around 20,000 contract and outsourced employees just before the peak summer season. The move severely reduced field manpower. A single sub-station typically handles eight feeders spread across villages located 30–35 km apart. Despite this large coverage area, only three teams are available to manage all eight feeders around the clock. Shutdown of power plants reduced supply by 3,000 MW Several power plants, including Anpara, Obra, Harduaganj, and Parichha, along with private-sector plants in Lalitpur and Prayagraj, suffered sudden technical failures in May. These units had to undergo “forced shutdowns” for periods ranging from three to eighteen days. As a result, Uttar Pradesh lost nearly 3,000 MW of electricity supply. Poor coordination and Delayed maintenance Avadhesh Verma further alleged that poor coordination between the Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation and the state generation corporation delayed maintenance work at several plants. Some private plants also failed to receive coal supplies on time, causing shortages and forcing production shutdowns. Critics claim the lack of coordination between the minister and the chairman delayed efforts to restore operations quickly. BJP MLAs bypassed the minister, wrote directly to CM As public anger grew over prolonged outages, BJP legislators began facing protests in their constituencies. Instead of approaching the energy minister, many MLAs directly contacted Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. Key complaints by BJP MLAs Several BJP legislators have openly compared AK Sharma unfavorably with former Energy Minister Shrikant Sharma, saying issues were resolved quickly during his tenure. Some MLAs reportedly complained that even contacting AK Sharma had become difficult. Why PMO and CMO experience failed in UP Senior journalists and political analysts believe AK Sharma’s long bureaucratic career did not translate into successful political and administrative management in Uttar Pradesh. The energy department has powerful employee unions, and structural reforms have remained incomplete. Earlier, employees staged protests over privatization plans. At one point, tensions between the energy minister and the Chief Minister reportedly became public when AK Sharma stated, I cannot transfer even a junior engineer on my own. Weak public communication became a major problem Political observers say one of AK Sharma’s biggest weaknesses is his distance from both the media and the public. He often leaves press conferences without answering journalists’ questions. During public protests over power cuts, critics say he sometimes responded with religious slogans instead of explaining solutions. At the same time, department officials and engineers also failed to communicate effectively with consumers regarding supply shortages. Gujarat’s “Feeder Model” could not be implemented in UP Senior journalist Virendranath Bhatt pointed out that Uttar Pradesh’s power generation capacity has doubled from 16,000 MW during the Samajwadi Party government to around 32,000 MW today. However, while the government expanded electricity connections, infrastructure upgrades did not keep pace. When Narendra Modi was Chief Minister of Gujarat, he improved electricity management by separating domestic and agricultural feeders. AK Sharma, who worked closely with Modi, was expected to replicate the model in Uttar Pradesh. Critics argue that even after five years, the Centre’s Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS) has not been effectively implemented in the state. Political performance also under scrutiny Municipal elections 2023: Defeat in home district In the Mau municipal elections, considered AK Sharma’s home turf, he reportedly insisted on fielding Dalit candidate Ajay Kumar despite the seat being unreserved. The BJP candidate eventually lost by 36,000 votes. Ghosi by-election 2023 In the Ghosi by-election, BJP deployed significant resources, but Sharma failed to consolidate Bhumihar voters in favor of the party. Candidate Dara Singh Chauhan lost the election. Lok Sabha elections 2024 During the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, Sharma was tasked with consolidating Bhumihar votes in the Kashi region. Post-election assessments suggested that a section of Bhumihar voters shifted toward Congress, reducing Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s victory margin in Varanasi.

stories.title: Truck crushes 6 including teacher to death in Banda:First runs over cyclist, then hits e-rickshaw
stories.summary: In Banda on Wednesday, a sand-laden truck ran over a retired teacher. After this, in an attempt to escape, it killed 5 more people. All of them were traveling by e-rickshaw. 5 other people were seriously injured. After the incident, angry villagers blocked the road and started protesting. Heavy police force has been deployed at the scene. Meanwhile, after the accident, the truck overturned, while the driver fled the scene. Police are searching for him. The matter pertains to the Bisanda police station area. First 3 pictures Now read the full story It was around 5 PM on Wednesday. Retired teacher Rameshwar (61), a resident of Ghuri village, was returning home from BRC. During this, a sand-laden truck coming at high speed from the Khurhand side ran over him. Rameshwar came under the truck. The wheel ran over his head, causing his death on the spot. People present there saw the accident and started chasing the truck. In response, the driver increased the truck's speed. About 2 km ahead, the truck went out of control. After this, the truck collided head-on with an e-rickshaw coming from the opposite direction on Oran Road. As a result, Mamta (48), Rakesh (45), Shahbaz (12), Sohanlal (50), and Naveen (40), residents of Korrahi village who were sitting in the e-rickshaw, died on the spot. Meanwhile, Sohanlal's wife Bauri (49), daughter Shivkali (17), and Shabana (40) along with her daughter Safiya (3 months) were seriously injured. Injured undergoing treatment in hospital After such a major accident, people's anger erupted. They blocked the road and started protesting. Upon receiving information, police and administrative officials reached the spot and pacified the people. With the help of local residents, the police sent the injured to the hospital. The condition of some of the injured is said to be serious. Considering the situation, heavy police force has been deployed in the area. The bodies have also been sent for post-mortem. DM Amit Aseri informed - On Bisanda-Oran Road, a truck driver first hit a cyclist, who died on the spot. After this, the driver started fleeing with the truck. After some distance, the truck lost control and hit an e-rickshaw. In this accident, three occupants of the e-rickshaw died on the spot, while two other injured individuals succumbed to their injuries during treatment. Treatment for four injured individuals is ongoing. Eyewitness Deepu Gupta said- A truck was coming from Banda Road. First, the driver ran the truck over a person, due to which he died. After this, the truck hit an e-rickshaw. This resulted in the death of people sitting in the e-rickshaw. A memorandum has been submitted regarding 'no-entry' here. There should be a 'no-entry' zone here. -

stories.title: 2 land dealers bodies found near college in Varanasi:Police launch probe with murder angle, poisonous material was found at scene
stories.summary: Two young men involved in land business in Varanasi were found dead under suspicious circumstances. Their bodies were found lying near the boundary behind Harishchandra Degree College in Baniyapur. It is being suspected that both young men were murdered and their bodies were brought and dumped here. Upon receiving information, police and forensic team reached the spot and started investigation. College staff spotted two bodies In the morning, when college staff reached the premises, they saw two bodies lying near the boundary. When police arrived after receiving information, a crowd of nearby villagers gathered. Police cordoned off the area and took it under their control and started collecting evidence. It has also come to light that a suspicious poisonous substance was found at the scene, which is being investigated. Both were involved in land business In the preliminary investigation, the deceased have been identified as Abhijit Ganguly, a resident of Nai Basti in Hukulgunj, and Nihal Singh, a resident of Kohasi in Cholapur. Both were associated with land business. According to the police, both had gone to see a relative's land. What happened to them after that has not yet been clarified. The police are investigating various angles to determine the motive behind the murder. Foul smell was emanating from the bodies According to police officials, both bodies appear to be old and a strong foul smell was coming from them. This raises suspicion that the deaths may have occurred one or two days ago. However, the exact time and cause of death will only be clear after the postmortem report arrives. DCP, ACP reached the spot As soon as information about the incident was received, DCP Varuna Pramod Kumar, ACP Sarnath Vidush Saxena, SO Cholapur and SOG team reached the spot. The officers inspected the scene and directed the forensic team to collect evidence. Police have taken both bodies into custody and after completing the panchnama, sent them for post-mortem. The relatives of the deceased have also reached the spot and are being questioned. Police investigating several points Police are trying to find out who the two youths were last in contact with and how they reached the scene. People in the vicinity are being questioned. Along with this, mobile call details and other technical evidence are also being examined.

stories.title: Inspector found hanging from window ventilator in Badaun:Body discovered in kneeling position, suicide suspected
stories.summary: A police inspector posted in court security was found hanging inside his rented room in Badaun on Thursday morning. The body was discovered hanging from a noose tied to the ventilator grill above the room's door. The inspector was found in a kneeling position. No suicide note was recovered from the scene. Superintendent of Police Ankita Sharma said the case appears to be a suicide prima facie, but the exact circumstances will be confirmed only after the post-mortem report and further investigation. Inspector had been living in the house for a year The deceased, Inspector Meghshyam Gautam (55), was posted in court security. He was a native of Sakna village in the Govindnagar police station area of Mathura and had been living in a rented room in Madhuban Colony under Nagar Kotwali police station limits for the past year. Police have seized his mobile phone and are examining call records. A forensic team also inspected the scene. See pictures- Daughter alerted landlord after calls went unanswered Landlord Vikesh said he owns a two-storey house and that Gautam lived on the first floor along with two other families. According to Vikesh, he was in his village when Gautam's daughter called him at around 9 am on Thursday. She said she had been trying to contact her father repeatedly but was unable to reach him. Vikesh informed his wife, who knocked on Gautam's door several times but received no response. He then returned home and informed the police. When police arrived and broke open the door, they found Gautam hanging inside the room. SP: Situation will become clear after post-mortem, family questioning SP Ankita Sharma said police received information at around 9:45 am about the incident. The body was found hanging from a noose made with a towel tied to the ventilator grill above the 6.5-foot-high door. "No suicide note has been found. The mobile phone has been seized and call details are being examined. The exact circumstances will become clear after questioning family members and receiving the post-mortem report," she said.

stories.title: UP govt transfers 206 police officers:Stuti Singh posted as Sambhal CO; Vikas Jaiswal joins CM security, Priyanka Bajpai shifted to Kanpur
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh government on Thursday transferred 206 Provincial Police Service (PPS) officers in a major administrative reshuffle. The transfers include a large number of officers who had been posted at the same station for an extended period, as well as several officers recently promoted from inspector to Circle Officer (CO). Deputy Superintendent of Police Jitendra Kumar-II, who was serving in the Chief Minister’s security detail, has been transferred to Shahjahanpur. Lucknow Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP) Vikas Kumar Jaiswal has been assigned to the Chief Minister’s security unit. The transfer of ACP Arvind Kumar-II from the Gautam Buddha Nagar Commissionerate to Lakhimpur Kheri has been cancelled, allowing him to continue in his current posting. Among other key transfers, Kannauj DSP Priyanka Bajpai has been posted as ACP in Kanpur, while Bijnor DSP Som Prakash Verma has been transferred to Mau. Agra ACP Sukanya Sharma has been appointed DSP of Baghpat, and Hapur DSP Stuti Singh has been posted as CO Sambhal. Lucknow ACP Satish Kumar Rai has been transferred to the Provincial Armed Constabulary (PAC) in Meerut. Rajeev Kumar Sisodia, CO of Railway Saharanpur, and Dr Ravi Shankar, CO of Muzaffarnagar, have been posted as ACPs in the Gautam Buddha Nagar Commissionerate. CM security gets new officer Deputy Superintendent of Police Jitendra Kumar-II, who was posted in the Chief Minister's security wing in Lucknow, has been transferred to Shahjahanpur. In his place, CO Vikas Kumar Jaiswal from Raebareli has been given the responsibility of the Chief Minister's security. In another decision, the government cancelled the transfer of ACP Arvind Kumar-II from Gautam Buddh Nagar Commissionerate to Kheri. He will continue in his current posting. Major changes in Lucknow and Noida commissionerates In Lucknow Commissionerate, Uday Pratap Singh-II from Gorakhpur, Rajesh Kumar Singh from Agra and Abhishek Kumar Pandey from Kanpur Nagar have been appointed as new ACPs. ACP Satish Kumar Rai has been transferred from Lucknow to PAC Meerut. In Gautam Buddh Nagar (Noida) Commissionerate, Rajiv Kumar Sisodiya from Railway Saharanpur and Dr Ravi Shankar from Muzaffarnagar have been posted as ACPs. Key transfers across districts and units Among the notable transfers, Anuruddh Kumar has been moved from Maharajganj to Mahoba, Abhishek Singh from Kaushambi to Balrampur, Ajay Kumar Shrotiya from Jhansi to Amroha and Pankaj Pant from Shahjahanpur to Rampur. Ashok Kumar Mishra-II has been shifted from Bhadohi to the 30th Battalion PAC in Gonda, while Manish Kumar Yadav has been transferred from Prayagraj Airport Security to the 4th Battalion PAC in Prayagraj. Several officers have also been posted to Varanasi Commissionerate, PAC battalions, LIU units and police training centres across the state. Women officers receive new postings The reshuffle also changed the jurisdictions of several women officers. Stuti Singh has been transferred from Hapur to Sambhal. Sarjana Singh has been moved from Aligarh and posted as Assistant Commandant of the 49th Battalion PAC in Gautam Buddh Nagar. Jyotishree has been transferred from Balrampur and appointed ACP in Kanpur Nagar Commissionerate. Shweta Verma has been posted as ACP in Agra Commissionerate from Mathura. Vineeta has been shifted from Hamirpur to Police Training School (PTS), Meerut. Shuchita Singh has been appointed ACP in Ghaziabad Commissionerate from Meerut. Immediate joining ordered The DGP Headquarters has directed all 206 transferred officers to immediately hand over charge and join their new postings. The order aims to ensure a smooth transition and prevent any disruption to law and order duties across the state. See the complete list...

stories.title: TGT exam enters second day in Gorakhpur:Candidates screened with metal detectors, over 18,000 set to appear
stories.summary: The second day of the Uttar Pradesh Trained Graduate Teacher (TGT) Recruitment Examination began on Thursday amid tight security arrangements across examination centres in Gorakhpur. Entry for the first shift started early in the morning, with candidates being allowed inside only after multiple levels of verification. Officials conducted screening through metal detectors, Aadhaar card verification and retina scans before permitting candidates to take their seats. Candidates were also seen checking their examination rooms and roll numbers outside the centres before entering. 15 centres in first shift, 24 in second A total of 15 examination centres have been set up for the first shift, while the second shift will be conducted at 24 centres across the city. Altogether, 18,188 candidates have registered for the examination on the second day. The first day's examination on Wednesday was completed peacefully without any disruption. Recruitment exam being held after four years The recruitment examination is being conducted after nearly four years and has attracted candidates from across Uttar Pradesh. The district administration and education department have made extensive arrangements to ensure smooth conduct of the examination. According to data released by the commission, 868,531 candidates have applied for 3,539 teaching posts. The examination is being held over two days, June 3 and 4, 2026. Documents required for entry Candidates must carry the following documents to the examination centre: Officials said candidates without the required documents could face difficulties in appearing for the examination. No negative marking The commission has confirmed that there will be no negative marking in the examination. As a result, candidates can attempt all questions without the risk of losing marks for incorrect answers. OMR sheets to be handled by invigilators Candidates will not be required to separate the copy of their OMR answer sheet after the examination. Invigilators will separate the answer sheet copy and hand it over to candidates. Gates to close 45 minutes before exam The commission has issued strict instructions regarding entry timings. No candidate will be allowed to enter the examination centre after the gates are closed. Tight security arrangements at all centres Authorities have strengthened security measures at all examination centres to ensure fair and peaceful conduct of the recruitment test. Special monitoring teams have also been deployed. Officials have advised candidates to follow all examination guidelines carefully and reach their centres well before the reporting time to avoid any inconvenience.

stories.title: Lucknow shines in IIRF 2026 rankings:IIM placed 5th, BBAU 19th; Law faculty secures 13th rank nationally
stories.summary: Lucknow's Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar University (BBAU) has secured the 19th rank among Central Universities in the Indian Institutional Ranking Framework (IIRF) 2026. The university's Department of Law also performed strongly, securing the 13th position at the national level. Meanwhile, IIM Lucknow was ranked fifth among management institutes in India. IIM Lucknow slips to fifth rank In the IIRF 2026 rankings, IIM Lucknow dropped one place from last year and secured the fifth position nationwide. The institute scored 94.74 points based on parameters such as research output, placements, alumni feedback, graduate outcomes, and employability. In the 2025 rankings, IIM Lucknow had secured the fourth rank. IIM Lucknow Director Prof. M.P. He said the ranking is the result of the combined efforts of the entire university community and expressed confidence that BBAU will continue to achieve greater success at both national and international levels. Established in 1996 Established in 1996, BBAU is one of the country's leading central universities. The institution offers undergraduate, postgraduate, and research programmes through its campuses in Lucknow and Amethi. Focus on research, innovation and inclusion The Vice Chancellor said the university remains focused on promoting quality education, research, innovation, and social inclusion. He added that these efforts have helped BBAU improve its performance in national rankings and strengthen its appeal among students across the country.

stories.title: Heavy rain lashes Meerut as UP braces for storm:Alert in 42 districts; winds may touch 80 kmph, Basti hottest at 42°C
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh has been witnessing thunderstorms and rain for the past 10 days. Intermittent rainfall was reported in Meerut on Thursday morning, while cloudy conditions prevailed across several districts of western Uttar Pradesh. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a thunderstorm and rain alert for 42 districts, warning of strong winds reaching speeds of 60-80 kmph and the possibility of lightning strikes. According to the weather department, pre-monsoon rainfall in the state has remained above normal since March 1. The southwest monsoon is expected to enter Uttar Pradesh between June 18 and 20 and may reach the state capital, Lucknow, by June 22. On Wednesday, districts including Kanpur, Gorakhpur and Azamgarh received rain accompanied by strong winds. Basti recorded the highest temperature in the state at 42°C. Western disturbance to influence weather till June 5 Lucknow-based meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said a fresh western disturbance became active over northwest India on Wednesday and is expected to affect the entire state by June 5. He said scattered rainfall is likely across western and eastern Uttar Pradesh, with isolated hailstorms also possible. Winds may gust up to 70 kmph, keeping temperatures in check and preventing heatwave conditions. Similar weather is expected to continue for the next three days. Five-day weather forecast for Uttar Pradesh City weather updates Meerut Weather conditions changed on Thursday morning, with rain and strong winds bringing relief from heat and humidity. The IMD expects similar conditions to persist for the next three days. Lucknow The city witnessed strong sunshine and humid conditions from the morning. The maximum temperature may touch 41°C today, while temperatures could cross 44°C over the next four days. Light clouds and isolated drizzle are possible on Friday, though they are unlikely to provide significant relief from the heat. Varanasi Light cloud cover was seen from the morning, although temperatures remained above 40°C. The city recorded 40.1°C, with a slight drop expected over the next 24 hours. Rainfall is also possible due to the active western disturbance. Environmental experts have noted the appearance of sandbars in several stretches of the Ganga River, attributing them to declining water levels and reduced river flow. Bareilly The city recorded bright sunshine and hot winds since morning. The maximum temperature is expected to reach 38°C, while the minimum may remain around 28°C. Monsoon may be weaker this year Meteorological officials have indicated that Uttar Pradesh could receive below-normal rainfall during the June-September monsoon season. Experts say the fading La Niña conditions and emerging El Niño pattern over the Pacific Ocean may weaken the southwest monsoon this year. Last year, Uttar Pradesh received around 870-900 mm of rainfall during the monsoon season, about 10-15% above the normal average.

stories.title: UP police reshuffle on cards:Renuka Mishra in line for DG Vigilance; two commissioners may be shifted
stories.summary: After the permanent appointment of DGP Rajeev Krishna, there were expectations that long-pending police postings would be cleared quickly. However, the transfer list remains on hold, with appointments to several senior posts, including DG, ADG and IG, yet to be finalised. According to sources, administrative factors have slowed the process. With Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath closely monitoring law and order, action against several SSPs and Police Commissioners is also being considered. The May 31 order confirming Rajeev Krishna as DGP did not mention the additional charge of the Vigilance Department that he had been holding. As a result, the DG Vigilance post is now technically vacant. DG Rules Manual post under discussion DG Rules Manual Antony Dev Kumar retired on May 31. Within the police department, the post is often viewed as a non-field assignment. Antony Dev Kumar, who was promoted from ADG to DG in March 2026, was nearing retirement and was therefore not given a major field posting. Renuka Mishra may be adjusted to vacant post There is speculation that 1990-batch IPS officer Renuka Mishra could be posted as DG Rules Manual. She is the senior-most IPS officer in Uttar Pradesh and was considered a contender for the DGP post. However, her prospects were affected by the constable recruitment paper leak controversy. In its report to the UPSC, the state government stated that a blacklisted company was awarded the paper-printing contract during her tenure as recruitment board chairperson. Following the controversy, she was attached to the DGP headquarters. Several senior posts await appointments CM reviews law and order performance Sources say the delay in the transfer list is also linked to the Chief Minister's review of recent law and order incidents. Officials believe changes in at least two police commissionerates and two district police units are likely in the next transfer order.

stories.title: 4 murders, ₹1.5 crore loot, and a deadly betrayal:Friend-turned-killer stayed with bodies for 12 hours; son's attack shattered father's skull into 10 pieces
stories.summary: Sunny Gupta, accused of killing four members of a wealthy businessman's family in Prayagraj, allegedly spent nearly 12 hours inside the house after the murders, trying to erase evidence before leaving. According to police, Sunny left the house around 5 am on June 1 and reached his home by 6:30 am. When family members questioned him about being away all night, he claimed he had been preparing kachoris for a wedding. He then went to his room and slept. To trace the accused, police scanned footage from nearly 150 CCTV cameras within a 2-km radius. One camera captured Sunny leaving the businessman's house. Investigators showed the footage to a kachori-samosa vendor operating near the residence, who identified him. Based on this lead, police arrested Sunny, who later confessed during questioning. Police also recovered jewellery worth about Rs 1.5 crore, allegedly looted from the house of businessman Virendra Kumar Vaishya. The postmortem report, received on June 3, revealed that Abhishek and his friend Sunny Gupta first killed Abhishek's sister. One bone in her skull was found fractured. They then allegedly murdered Abhishek's parents, with around 10 skull fractures found on each of them. Investigators said Sunny later killed Abhishek as well and allegedly poured toilet cleaner on his face in an attempt to destroy evidence. The postmortem found 12 injury marks on Abhishek's body. Meanwhile, two police inspectors have been suspended for alleged negligence in connection with the case. Police scanned 150 CCTV cameras to trace accused Investigators examined footage from nearly 150 CCTV cameras across a 2-km radius, from South Malaka to Mahaviran Gali, to crack the quadruple murder case. One camera captured accused Sunny Gupta leaving businessman Virendra Kumar Vaishya's house around 5 am on June 1. Further analysis showed Sunny entering the house with Vaishya's son Abhishek around 3 pm on May 31. Another footage later showed him returning to his home in Mutthiganj after leaving the Vaishya residence. Brother had reported him missing Sunny's family grew concerned when he failed to return home on the night of May 31 and his mobile phone remained switched off. His brother Manoj informed South Malaka police station that Sunny was missing, but no immediate action was taken. When Sunny returned home on June 1, his brother asked where he had been. Sunny claimed he had spent the night preparing kachoris at a wedding and would earn Rs 5,000 for the work. He then went to sleep. Postmortem reveals brutal killings The postmortem of businessman Virendra Kumar Vaishya, his wife Anita, daughter Meenakshi and son Abhishek was conducted on June 3. According to the report, Abhishek and Sunny first attacked Meenakshi, leaving a skull fracture. They then killed Virendra and Anita, repeatedly striking their heads with an iron rod. Doctors found multiple fractures in both victims' skulls. Police said Sunny later turned on Abhishek and killed him with the same weapon. The postmortem found several fractures and injury marks on his chest, arms, legs and face. Investigators said Sunny poured toilet cleaner on Abhishek's face and later attempted to erase evidence by cleaning blood stains inside the house. He reportedly stayed in the house overnight, bathed there and left around 5 am on June 1. Now read what came in the postmortem report On June 3, the postmortem of Virendra Kumar Vaishya, his wife Anita, daughter Meenakshi, and son Abhishek was conducted. According to the report, Abhishek brutally killed his parents. He struck their heads more than 12 times. This shattered the front, back, and middle bones of both their skulls. Meanwhile, sister Meenakshi was found with only one front bone broken. After the 3 murders, Sunny Gupta also brutally killed Abhishek. He struck Abhishek repeatedly with an iron rod. This resulted in his skull bones also being broken. Additionally, injuries were found on his chest, arms, legs, and face. After committing the murders, Sunny poured toilet cleaner on Abhishek's face. This caused his face to be scorched. After the 4 murders, Sunny cleaned the blood stains from the stairs and rooms. He bathed in the bathroom. After this, he slept in the house itself. About 12 hours later, he left the businessman's house around 5 AM on the morning of June 1. Police Commissioner suspends two officers The investigation has also revealed alleged negligence by police. On the night of May 31, Sunny Gupta's brother informed police that he was missing and his phone was switched off. Officials later found lapses in the response to the information. Following the inquiry, Police Commissioner Jogendra Kumar suspended South Malaka outpost in-charge Rohit Kumar Gaud and Senior Sub-Inspector Mulayam Yadav of Kotwali police station. The case at a glance Virendra Kumar Vaishya ran a gift business and lived with his family in a two-storey house at Heewet Road crossing in Prayagraj. The 8,000 sq ft property, estimated to be worth Rs 10-15 crore, has 14 shops on the ground floor, 13 of which are rented out. Virendra lived on the upper floor with his wife Anita, daughter Meenakshi and son Abhishek. Meenakshi managed a gift shop in the building, while Abhishek dealt in pesticides and floor-cleaning products. Both siblings were unmarried. The couple's younger son, Ashwini, is lodged in Kaushambi jail. His wife Ritu is currently out on bail and staying at her parental home in Kidganj. On June 2, the bodies of Virendra (70), Anita (65) and Meenakshi (45) were found inside the locked house. Around two hours later, the body of Abhishek (40) was recovered from a shop on the ground floor. That shop was also locked from outside. Abhishek often clashed with his father Police said Abhishek had a strained relationship with his father. Neighbours and relatives told investigators that disputes over money and business matters were common in the family. According to the probe, Abhishek had previously borrowed several lakh rupees and failed to repay the amount on time. The lender allegedly assaulted him and threatened the family. His sister Meenakshi later arranged the money and secured his release, leading to further tensions between Abhishek and his father. A mansion left without an heir The Vaishya family's wealth included a prime 8,000 sq ft property and 14 shops generating rental income worth several lakh rupees every month. With Virendra, Anita, Meenakshi and Abhishek dead, and the younger son in jail, there is currently no immediate family member living in the house. Police reconstruction of the crime Six questions that still remain unanswered Despite the police explanation, several questions continue to raise doubts.

stories.title: 21 UP highways set for four-lane upgrade:Speed limit to rise from 80 to 100 kmph; major boost for East UP
stories.summary: 21 state highways in UP will become four-lane. This work will be completed by December 2027. The Public Works Department has completed the survey of these roads passing through 18 districts. The proposal has been sent to the state government. The state government is improving state highways along with expressways and national highways. There are 142 state highways in UP. 107 state highways have been widened up to 10 meters. In the second phase, 21 state highways are being made four-lane. After this work is completed, the remaining 14 state highways will also be made four-lane. On these four-lane highways, vehicles will run at a maximum speed of 90-100 km. Earlier they used to run at a speed of 70-80 km. Now the journey will not only be comfortable, but will also be completed quickly. 3 state highways of Varanasi, 2 of Hardoi will be developed Among the 21 state highways in the state, 3 roads from Varanasi and 2 from Hardoi are included. Apart from this, roads from Amethi, Sultanpur, Pratapgarh, Deoria, Kushinagar, Jalaun, Farrukhabad, Lucknow, Moradabad, Bulandshahr, Meerut, Sonbhadra, Sambhal, Muzaffarnagar, Chandauli and Jaunpur have been included. In this way, around 18 districts are going to benefit. Here the roads are 7 to 14 meters wide, but now they will be widened from 14 to 25 meters. First, know about the 9 roads that will become four-lane... Jagdishpur Road- This 28-kilometer long road connects Amethi to Sultanpur, Pratapgarh and Raebareli. 639 crore rupees will be spent on its widening. Bahraich-Bhinga-Sirsia-Chaudhary Deeh Road- About 21 kilometers of road will be widened. 46 crore rupees will be spent on this. Deoria-Padrauna Highway- This 31-kilometer road will be made four-lane for better connectivity to Kushinagar International Airport and Agricultural University. 292 crores will be spent on this. Panwari Highway (Jalaun)- This road is 53 kilometers long. Work on this road started 10 years ago. After some portion was built, the work stopped. Now 223 crores will be spent to complete it. Bilgram-Unnao-Prayagraj Route- The length of this road is 90 kilometers. Preparations are underway to upgrade it to a National Highway. 5442 crore rupees will be spent. BSA State Highway in Hardoi- More road accidents occur on this highway. About 67 crore rupees are being spent on this approximately 11 kilometer long route. Its construction is ongoing. Three Routes in Varanasi- Chaubeypur Road, Varanasi-Kachwa Road and Kachwa-Chaubeypur Road are being made four-lane. PWD has not made public how much budget is being spent on this. Four-lane highway will have many hi-tech facilities Four-lane roads are designed in such a way that the speed of vehicles remains at 90 to 100 km/hour. This will make the journey comfortable. Bikes can also run on these. Their high speed remains 80-90 km/hour. Compared to normal 2-lane roads, many modern facilities are provided on four-lane roads. These are different based on safety and infrastructure. Know these too... Rumble strips will wake up sleeping drivers Safe Divider- There is a divider in the middle to separate traffic from both sides. Plants are grown on it, so that at night the headlight beams from oncoming vehicles do not fall on the eyes. Crash Barrier- There are strong barriers made of steel or concrete on the sides of the road and on the divider. This prevents any vehicle from going out of control and falling off the road or going to the other side. Rumble Strips- White colored raised strips are made on the road before toll plazas, junctions or accidental zones. These cause vibrations in vehicles, which wake up sleeping drivers. Reflectors- Reflective reflectors are installed in the middle and on the sides of the road to show the way at night or during fog. Service Lane for Local Traffic Service Road- A separate service lane is provided for local traffic of villages or towns situated along the highway. This ensures that local vehicles do not disturb the speed of the main highway. Underpass and Overpass- Underpasses are constructed for local residents, animals, and vehicles to cross from one side to the other. This eliminates the risk of accidents on the highway. Bypass- To avoid traffic jams in big cities, a bypass is created outside the cities. Drainage System- To prevent rainwater from accumulating on the road, paved drains are built on both sides. This prevents the road from deteriorating quickly. Parking for Trucks Truck Parking- To prevent trucks from parking on the roadside, separate large parking spaces are created. These have facilities for toilets and rest rooms. Petrol Pump, Restaurant- For travelers, petrol pumps, restaurants, dhabas, toilets, and vehicle repair shops are developed at fixed distances. Help Available Every 2 km in Case of Accident Emergency Calling Box- In case of any accident or vehicle breakdown, SOS boxes or helpline numbers are provided every 1-2 kilometers for assistance. Ambulance and Crane Service- In case of toll roads, the highway authority's quick response team, ambulances, and patrolling vehicles continuously make rounds. Smart Sign Boards- Reflective sign boards are installed that provide information about speed limits, upcoming turns, and routes.

stories.title: Awareness campaign on World No Tobacco Day in Gorakhpur:Divyangjan took oath of de-addiction, health kits and umbrellas distributed
stories.summary: On the occasion of World No Tobacco Day on Saturday, an awareness program for persons with disabilities was organized under the leadership of social worker and teacher Gyanendra Ojha in Gorakhpur. In the program, people were informed about serious diseases caused by tobacco and smoking and motivated to stay away from its consumption. During the program, participants were told that consumption of tobacco and smoking can cause serious diseases like cancer of the mouth, throat, lips, and lungs. Besides this, information was also given about heart disease, damage to blood vessels, and the adverse effects on the health of pregnant women and the fetus. Handbills were distributed among persons with disabilities to raise awareness. Pledge taken to adopt a healthy lifestyle Highlighting the importance of World No Tobacco Day, those present were made to take an oath to stay away from smoking and tobacco products. The speakers said that only by maintaining distance from tobacco can one avoid many serious diseases and live a healthy life. In the program, State Advisory Board member Umesh Chandra Kiran, along with other differently-abled persons, was also honored. On this occasion, umbrellas, towels, and health kits were distributed for protection from heat and heat stroke. Those honored included Laxmi Prajapati, Bharat Lal, Nandkishore, Arvind Gupta, Jyoti Kumari, Chhaya Prajapati, and Mahesh Kumar, among others. Red Cross members provided support In making the program successful, Indian Red Cross Society's lifetime members Vinay Kumar Pathak, Shikha Pandey, Sanjeev Kumar Rai, Mahendra Pratap Pandey, and Aditya Nigam, along with others, provided support. The organizers expressed gratitude towards all the supporters.

stories.title: Mother demands death penalty after toddler brutally killed:Police arrest suspect after encounter; family alleges murder was linked to one-sided love
stories.summary: 'My son's murderer should be given the death penalty. If no one can punish him, then hand him over to me. We will tear him apart and kill him.' This is the grief and anger of a mother from Firozabad, whose one-and-a-half-year-old child was killed by being slammed repeatedly on Saturday. The murderer, Viraj, was in one-sided love with the child's mother. A video of him has surfaced, in which he is lying on a stretcher after an encounter, desperately asking for water. He is repeatedly asking the police for water. The 'Dainik Bhaskar' app team reached the victim's family on Sunday. The child's mother and grandmother expressed their pain. They accused the child's father and in-laws of orchestrating the murder. Read the report Rati's wedding took place in the year 2024 Bamai village is 45 kilometers away from the Firozabad headquarters. The village is Rati's maternal home. She was married to Suneet, a resident of Siyaran Nagar, Badaun, on February 18, 2024, but there is a family dispute going on between the husband and wife. Due to this, Rati had been living at her maternal home since January 2025. She used to occasionally visit her in-laws' house as well. One-and-a-half-year-old son Aarav was born at his maternal grandparents' home. When the team reached Rati's maternal home, there was a crowd of people outside the house. Everyone was talking about the incident. Village women were consoling Rati. Aarav's grandmother, Pinky, was sitting in a corner crying. Mother said - He took my baby away in front of me Rati said, I had gone to meet my friend Pushpalata Pathak in Yadav Colony. Pushpalata had recently been injured in a road accident. Around three in the afternoon, my husband Suneet's aunt's son Viraj alias Jitendra Pathak arrived there. Viraj told me that he would get toffee for Babu, but he killed my son. After committing the murder, he left my child at the gate and fled. My in-laws have had my son murdered. Husband used to say - Not my son, get DNA test done Rati said, "My in-laws had thrown me out of the house. The in-laws used to say kill Aarav. My husband did not consider Aarav as his son. He used to say, " Get a DNA test done''. Rati said, after the incident, when I called and informed my husband, Suneet, about Aarav's death, he told me that you people were on the radar. When they couldn't kill you, they killed Aarav. Since coming to my maternal home, Viraj had been after me. He kept telling me to marry him. I refused, but he kept pursuing me. He was also in league with those people. How will we live without our beloved - Grandmother Rati's mother, Pinky, says, "My daughter's in-laws are in Badaun. Viraj used to say that he was on our side. But he was colluding with them, lying to us. My daughter used to go to her in-laws' place from time to time, but every time she was mistreated''. With great difficulty, we had saved and brought back our daughter and grandson. But Viraj killed our grandson. Now, how will we live without our beloved? Veeraj slammed Aarav 8 times The CCTV footage of the incident also surfaced. In which you can see that the accused comes carrying the child in his arms. Then suddenly throws him on the road. Then picks him up and throws him down again. The accused does this 8 times. After that, the youth picks up the child in his arms and looks around. He runs away and leaves the body outside the house and goes away. 2 pictures of the accused Police arrested the accused by shooting him in the leg On Saturday evening, police received input that the accused Viraj Bhudha was roaming near Bharthra Mod. When police reached the spot and tried to stop him, he started firing. In self-defense, police also fired shots. The accused fell down after being shot in both legs. Police recovered a 315 bore pistol, two empty cartridges, and 5 live cartridges from the accused. The injured accused was admitted to the district hospital. SP City Ravishankar Prasad said that the accused is being interrogated. CO Amarish Kumar said that the accused wanted to marry the woman. However, the woman had refused. The woman's relationship with her husband was not good. He was pressuring her for marriage. The accused felt that as long as she had her child, their marriage could not happen, which is why he targeted and killed the child.

stories.title: Rajiv Krishna becomes permanent DGP of UP:Government issues order; Renuka Mishra, Piyush Anand left behind
stories.summary: After a 4-year wait, UP has got a permanent DGP (Director General of Police). The current acting DGP, Rajeev Krishna, has been made the permanent DGP. Dainik Bhaskar had confirmed his name on Saturday (30th May) itself. On Sunday, ACS Sanjay Prasad issued the order on behalf of the UP government. According to UPSC guidelines and Supreme Court rules, he will remain UP's DGP for at least 2 years. Rajeev Krishna has been handling the charge of acting DGP since June 1, 2025. Actually, the UP government had sent names of 19 IPS officers to the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) for the permanent DGP post. A meeting of the commission was held in Delhi on 26th May regarding this. UP's Chief Secretary SP Goyal and Additional Chief Secretary Sanjay Prasad also participated in it. In the meeting, the names of Renuka Mishra, Piyush Anand, and Rajeev Krishna were finalized for the DGP panel. After this, the commission sent all three names to the UP government. Know about Rajeev Krishna Rajeev Krishna is a 1991 batch IPS officer. Originally a resident of Noida, Rajeev Krishna was born on June 26, 1969. He belongs to a family where there are not just one or two but more than 6 officers. His wife is an IRS officer. Currently, she is Deputy Secretary in the CBDT in Noida. Postings at various places After becoming an IPS officer in 1991, Rajeev Krishna's first posting as a trainee IPS was in Allahabad (now Prayagraj). After that, he was posted as an ASP in Bareilly, Kanpur, and Aligarh. On March 10, 1997, he was given command of a district for the first time and became SP of Firozabad. After that, he served as SSP of Etawah, Mathura, Fatehgarh, Bulandshahr, Gautam Buddh Nagar, Agra, Lucknow, and Bareilly. During Mayawati's tenure, when DIGs were being posted in large districts instead of SSPs, Rajeev Krishna was made DIG of Lucknow. Rajeev Krishna also became IG of Meerut Range. In 2012, he went on central deputation. When he returned in September 2017, he was first posted at the Police Academy in Moradabad. Then, on February 5, 2018, he was made ADG of Lucknow Zone. Rajeev Krishna also served as ADG Zone in the Agra Zone for two and a half years. After that, he was made acting DGP. Rajeev Krishna has a strong background Rajeev Krishna's family has had an influential presence in civil services (IPS, IRS) and politics for two generations. His wife, Meenakshi Singh, is Deputy Secretary in the CBDT in Noida. MLA from Sarojininagar, Rajeshwar Singh, is his brother-in-law. Rajeshwar Singh was an officer of the 1996 batch of UP Police. Later, he went on deputation to the Enforcement Directorate and merged into the same cadre. Just before the 2022 elections, Rajeshwar Singh took VRS and entered politics. He is currently an MLA from the Sarojininagar seat in Lucknow. Rajeshwar's wife, Laxmi Singh, is the Police Commissioner of Gautam Buddh Nagar. Besides this, his father-in-law was also a DIG. Will remain permanent DGP for at least 2 years According to UPSC guidelines and Supreme Court rules, after becoming permanent DGP, Rajeev Krishna's tenure will be at least 2 years. However, his original service period is until June 2029. If he remains permanent DGP for the next 2 years, then adding the one-year acting tenure, he will become the only officer in recent times to hold this highest position for a total of 3 years. UPSC panel had sent these 3 names UPSC had sent a panel of 3 officers to the UP government based on seniority. At the top was the name of Renuka Mishra (1990 batch). She has been without any charge for the past 2 years and is attached to the DGP office. The second name was Piyush Anand (1991 batch). He is currently on central deputation and serving as DG of NDRF (National Disaster Response Force). The third name was Rajeev Krishna (1991 batch), for whom the Yogi government issued orders on Sunday. The permanent DGP post was vacant for 4 years The permanent DGP post in UP had been vacant for the past 4 years. On May 11, 2022, the government removed the then full-time DGP Mukul Goyal, and since then, the state has been getting only acting DGPs. After Mukul Goyal's removal, DS Chauhan was made acting DGP. After that, RK Vishwakarma was made acting DGP for two months. After RK Vishwakarma, Vijay Kumar, and after Vijay Kumar, Prashant Kumar became acting DGP. Prashant Kumar retired on May 31 last year. Then, on June 1, 2025, Rajeev Krishna was made acting DGP.

stories.title: Wife of murdered businessman demands strict punishment:Family alleges repeated extortion threats were ignored, says, 'police failed to prevent murder'
stories.summary: “My Husband was killed, the accused should face the same fate”: Widow seeks justice after Ghazipur murder Aditi Rai, the wife of murdered businessman Vineet Rai, has demanded strict action against the accused, saying they should be punished in the same manner in which her husband was killed. "What was my fault that I was made a widow? My 3-month-old child has been left fatherless. What did the accused gain from this? Just as my innocent husband was shot dead, they too should face the same fate. The same number of bullets that struck my husband should be fired at them," she said, appealing to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath to ensure the culprits are not spared. Vineet Rai, son of hotel businessman Alok Rai, was shot dead late Friday night in Ghazipur. According to the family, four masked assailants surrounded him near the gate of the family hotel around midnight and opened fire. The murder has left the family devastated. Aditi, Vineet’s parents and other relatives have been inconsolable since the incident. His mother, overcome with grief, has repeatedly demanded that the accused be punished in the same way her son was killed, saying only then would she feel justice had been served. Meanwhile, Vineet’s father, Alok Rai, has warned that he and his family will resort to self-immolation in front of the Chief Minister if the accused are not arrested and strict action is not taken against them. On Sunday, the Dainik Bhaskar team reached their home in Gausabad and spoke with them. Father says - Accused have demanded extortion money several times The distance between deceased Vineet Rai's home and the crime scene, i.e., the hotel, is about 2 kilometres. When the team reaches the home, some people are found sitting outside the house. These people had come to console the deceased's father. During the conversation, father Alok Rai, controlling his tears, says that after completing his studies, his son was handling the entire business. He was getting the hotel renovated. I have been in the hotel business for 12 years. He explains that in the year 2024, some boys from the city and members of the Katra gang were sitting and drinking beer in our hotel's beer bar. During this time, an argument broke out between them. Then our hotel staff and family members intervened and drove both parties away from there. Since then, we have been the target of those boys. They had vandalised the hotel several times. They used to roam around in gangs and clash with someone or the other. Their name also came up in the Kumar murder case. From the year 2024 till today, I have sent complaints two to three times through registered post to all officers, including the DGP, Chief Minister, the Home Secretary, the Home Ministry, the ADG and the SP. I have already informed the police officers that the boys of the Katra gang create anarchy. It has 25-30 active members. He alleged that many people in the police force provide them protection. If the accused is not encountered, I will self-immolate in front of the CM The father said that the gang had once demanded extortion from us. We kept ignoring their demand. Later, they demanded ₹1 crore. They threatened that the amount would keep increasing for as many days as the money was not paid. He said that the price of the hotel is approximately ₹20 crore, so they want a large amount. Complained to the police, but neither the kotwal nor the local police nor the district officials took it seriously. If the police had taken my complaint seriously, my son would be alive. He said that the son is gone, but if the criminals are not encountered, we will self-immolate with the entire family in front of the Chief Minister. Younger brother narrated the story of the night of the murder... Father's younger brother Aadesh was also sitting there. Aadesh explains that since the hotel renovation work has been going on, I was staying at the hotel itself. On Friday night, I was at the hotel. I was standing in front of the first-floor gate. Brother Vineet was going outside the gate. Just then, suddenly, the sound of gunshots was heard. When I ran there, I saw Shankar Pandey and his associates running away. Brother was drenched in blood, staggering and trying to come inside the hotel, but fell on the porch. I called everyone while screaming. We took our brother to the district hospital. But the doctor declared him dead. Aadesh's voice chokes while narrating all this. The entire family is scared... Aadesh further says that earlier too, Shankar Pandey, Kamlesh Chaudhary, Sonu Yadav and Monu Tripathi had come to our hotel with their friends and threatened us. They used to demand extortion money from us. They kept threatening that if we want to do business, we will have to pay them extortion money. Sometimes they demanded ₹20 lakhs, sometimes ₹30 lakhs, sometimes ₹50 lakhs and sometimes even up to ₹1 crore. We never agreed to their demands. But now we are all scared. Who knows when someone might be attacked? They can target my father and me, too. No trace of accused even after 21 hours Meanwhile, even after more than 24 hours since the murder, no clues about the attackers have been found. They are currently out of police reach. However, police are interrogating four people in custody. The police captain has placed city kotwal Mahendra Singh on line duty. SP Dr. Iraj Raja has deployed four teams for the arrest of the accused. According to the SP, continuous raids and searches are being conducted to find the accused. DIG Vaibhav Krishna said that strict action will be taken against the criminal, whoever it may be.

stories.title: 12 B.Ed aspirants fall into drain near exam centre:Candidates pulled out by bystanders in Kanpur; AI cameras sent 6,000 alerts in 2 hrs
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Joint B.Ed Entrance Examination is being held today (Sunday) across 72 districts of the state. The first shift concluded at noon, while the second shift is scheduled to begin at 2 PM. Strict security measures are in place at examination centres. Candidates are being allowed entry only after verification of their Aadhaar card, admit card, photograph, facial identity, and retina scan. Watches and shoes are also being removed during the checking process. In Kanpur, ahead of the second shift, around 10–12 candidates fell into a drain after a portion of it collapsed near Prof. H.N. Mishra PG College. Their clothes were damaged, and some admit cards got wet. Fellow candidates and bystanders quickly helped pull them out. No injuries were reported. The examination is being monitored from a control room at Bundelkhand University, Jhansi, using around 20,000 AI-enabled cameras installed at centres. Between 9 AM and 11 AM, the system generated more than 6,000 alerts. State Coordinator Prof. Saurabh Srivastava said the alerts prompted calls to the concerned centres, directing officials to inspect examination rooms and verify the situation. The AI system sends alerts in cases of excessive crowding, unusual movement, or inactivity inside classrooms. To ensure the smooth conduct of the examination, the university has deployed 167 representatives across districts for monitoring. Bundelkhand University is conducting the Joint B.Ed Entrance Examination for the fourth consecutive year. A total of 4,44,958 candidates registered for the exam. See 4 pictures

stories.title: Surya’s mother demanded encounter for killers:Says, ‘I’ve lost everything’; calls for bulldozer action, warns of protest in Ghaziabad
stories.summary: "My successful son is gone. First, I lost my husband, now I have lost my son. I do not know what is written in my fate. My second son is often ill. God has shown me no mercy." These were the words of Saroj, the mother of 17-year-old Surya Chauhan, while speaking to Dainik Bhaskar on Saturday evening. She had demanded strict action against those responsible for her son's murder, saying the main accused should be killed in a police encounter and his house demolished. Within 12 hours of that conversation, Ghaziabad Police killed the main accused, Asad, in an encounter. After hearing the news, Saroj said she wanted proof. "I have only heard that one person has been killed. I want to see Asad's photograph. Only after seeing the picture will I feel satisfied," she said. She also demanded similar action against the remaining accused. "Seven people were involved in killing my son. The others should also face the same fate. Bulldozers should be used against all their houses," she said. When asked whether she planned to meet Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, Saroj replied: "We will not say anything now. We will speak when we go." Funeral held after nearly 10 hours of protests Earlier on Saturday, Surya's last rites were performed after nearly 10 hours of protests and unrest. The Class 11 student was stabbed near his home in Navneet Vihar under the Khoda police station area on Bakrid. According to a minor friend, the accused called Surya to meet him to settle an old rivalry. The friend alleged that the attackers asked Surya, "Have you ever seen a goat being slaughtered?" before repeatedly stabbing him. Following the murder, Dainik Bhaskar spoke to Surya's family members and neighbours, who described their grief and anger. 'Everything I had has been destroyed' Surya's father, Kaushalendra, a resident of Sukhwada village in Etah district, had passed away several years ago. For the past five years, Saroj had been living in a rented house in Navneet Vihar, Ghaziabad, near the Delhi border, with her two sons, Yash Chauhan and Surya Chauhan. Saroj works as an attendant at a private school. Her elder son, Yash, suffers from seizures and frequently falls ill. Before the encounter of the main accused, Saroj had told Dainik Bhaskar that she felt her entire world had collapsed. Crying repeatedly during the conversation, she said the people responsible for her son's death should be dealt with strictly. She also appealed to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath for employment assistance, saying the family was struggling financially. "My successful son is gone. My other son is unwell. I have lost everything," she said. Several times during the interview, her health deteriorated as she recalled memories of Surya. 'Mum, it's a holiday today' Recalling her last conversation with her son, Saroj said Surya had spoken to her on the morning of May 28. "He never went anywhere without informing me. Whenever he stepped out, he would call and tell me where he was going," she said. “On the morning of Bakrid, he told me, 'Mum, it's a holiday today, don't go anywhere.'” She said Surya and his elder brother had tea together that morning and later bought some household items from a nearby shop. "Then suddenly, in the afternoon, Asad called him. Surya was with two of his friends. He did not go to anyone's house. After that, those people stabbed my son to death in the middle of the road," she said. Neighbours demanded strict action Before Asad's encounter, neighbour Diksha said local residents were demanding the harshest possible action against those responsible. "The boys killed our Surya. Tomorrow they could kill someone else. We want justice. The murderer should be dealt with firmly," she said. After news of the encounter emerged, another neighbour, Ankit, said action against the remaining accused should continue. "It is good that the main accused has been caught and action has been taken, but our other demands should also be met. The remaining accused should also face the law, and their properties should be seized," he said. What happened on the day of the murder? According to Surya's minor friend, the incident took place on the afternoon of May 28. Asad, who lived around 300 metres from Surya's rented home, called him and asked whether he had ever seen a goat being slaughtered on Bakrid. Surya replied that he had no reason to see such a thing. He then went to the area near a banana warehouse in Lane No. 2 with two friends. The friend alleged that Asad and his associates, Nawab, Farhan, Atif and Sarik, were waiting there. They allegedly told Surya that they would show him a goat sacrifice before attacking him with knives. Severely injured and covered in blood, Surya collapsed. His friend attempted to stop the bleeding by tying a shirt around his wounds. Surya was later admitted to a hospital in Noida, where he died during treatment on May 29. Protest lasted for 10 hours Following Surya's death, more than 500 people gathered on the streets on Saturday morning and staged protests. The crowd demanded strict action against the accused and initially refused to allow the cremation to take place. The protest continued for nearly 10 hours before senior police officers persuaded the family and local residents to end the agitation. At around 6 pm, Surya's cremation was carried out at the Ghazipur crematorium in Delhi under police supervision. 8-month-old dispute emerges as possible motive Friends of the deceased claim that the murder may have stemmed from an incident around eight months ago. According to them, Surya had intervened during a dispute involving Asad and another young man. Since then, Asad allegedly held a grudge and often spoke about taking revenge. The family believes this earlier dispute led to the killing. Police are investigating all possible angles and are using CCTV footage and surveillance to track the remaining accused. Main accused dead, three arrested, one still absconding An FIR was registered against five people, including Asad, on the complaint of Surya's elder brother, Yash Chauhan. So far, police have arrested three accused. The main accused, Asad, has been killed in a police encounter, while one accused remains absconding.

stories.title: 'Quit party posts before seeking assembly ticket', says Akhilesh:Four leaders resigned so far; SP chief played same move during 2024 LS elections
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party (SP) chief Akhilesh Yadav recently held a major party meeting in which he made it clear that leaders and organisational office-bearers wishing to contest the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections must first resign from their current posts. He instructed such leaders to submit their names to the party high command, which will take the final decision on candidature. Following the directive, three senior party leaders have already resigned from their posts, while another is reportedly preparing to step down. Sources within the party say that many leaders keen to contest the 2027 elections are sending proposals to the national president, seeking consideration for tickets. As a result, several office-bearers are preparing to resign in the coming months. Akhilesh warns leaders not to 'guarantee' tickets On April 2, Akhilesh Yadav chaired a major meeting at the SP headquarters in Lucknow. District presidents and office-bearers from all 75 districts attended. During the meeting, he warned district presidents against acting as intermediaries or guaranteeing election tickets for any leader. He reportedly said that any complaint regarding such practices would invite disciplinary action. Akhilesh also made it clear that any district president wishing to contest an election must first resign from the post before the party considers their candidature. He said- If any district president wants to contest elections, they must resign first. Only then will the party consider their claim. No district president should declare themselves a candidate. That would be wrong. Three major reasons behind the decision 1. Reducing internal rivalries According to party insiders, when district presidents or office-bearers seek tickets while holding organisational positions, it often creates resentment among other local leaders. This can lead to factionalism within the party and affect voter mobilisation during elections. By asking aspirants to relinquish their posts, the party hopes to reduce internal conflicts. 2. Ensuring organisational work is not affected Akhilesh Yadav is believed to view a strong organisation as the key to electoral success. If office-bearers become occupied with their own election campaigns, party management at the district level may weaken. Separating organisational responsibilities from electoral ambitions is intended to keep the party machinery functioning effectively. 3. Narrowing the vote gap with the BJP In the 2022 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) secured approximately 8.5 million more votes than the Samajwadi Party. Party strategists believe that reducing internal disputes and improving coordination could help narrow, or even eliminate, that gap in the 2027 elections. SP wants a clear and conflict-free ticket distribution process Senior journalist Siddharth Kalahans said the Samajwadi Party has already set its sights firmly on returning to power in 2027. According to him, Akhilesh Yadav wants to avoid confusion, lobbying and internal disputes over ticket distribution this time. The party is reportedly following a "One Leader, One Post" approach, under which candidates with the strongest electoral prospects will be selected. Those chosen will be expected to focus solely on their constituencies and voter outreach rather than organisational responsibilities. Kalahans noted that resigning from a party post may strengthen a leader's claim for a ticket, but it does not guarantee selection. He said the party ultimately considers a range of electoral factors, including caste equations, local dynamics and the strength of rival candidates, before finalising nominations. Similar formula used in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections According to Siddharth Kalahans, Akhilesh Yadav had already tested a similar strategy during the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. At the time, then, state president Naresh Uttam Patel resigned from his organisational role to contest the election from Fatehpur. He went on to win the seat. Party leaders now view that experiment as successful, and the same model is being expanded across Uttar Pradesh in preparation for the 2027 Assembly elections.

stories.title: Heavy rain lashes UP, hailstorm hits Amroha:Rain follows dust storm in Lucknow; Tin shed falls on biker
stories.summary: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a rain alert for all 75 districts of Uttar Pradesh on Sunday. Hail accompanied rain in Amroha during the afternoon. Heavy rain along with strong winds was reported in Lucknow, Sambhal, Moradabad, Hathras, Gonda, and Balrampur. In Ballia, rain followed a dust storm. Over the next few hours, strong winds, rain, and hail are likely in 19 districts, including Shahjahanpur, Firozabad, Farrukhabad, Aligarh, and Bulandshahr. Wind speeds of 60 to 80 kmph may be recorded in these districts. In Lakhimpur Kheri, a 7-year-old child died on Sunday afternoon after a mud wall collapsed during a strong storm and rain. In Rampur, on Saturday evening, an iron tin shed from a hotel was uprooted during a storm and fell on a biker, seriously injuring him. CCTV footage of the incident has also surfaced. See 5 pictures- Amid storms and rain continuing for the past three days, the temperature has dropped by 10°C and come down to around 38°C. In the last 24 hours, the highest temperature in the state was recorded in Moradabad at 38.5°C. Just two days ago, on May 28, Banda had recorded a temperature of 47.5°C. According to the Meteorological Department, light rain is likely across the state tomorrow, June 1, as well. Cool winds will blow, and the sky will remain cloudy. Relief from the heat is expected to continue. The weather is likely to change again from June 2, with temperatures rising by 4°C to 5°C. However, no heatwave conditions are expected. Moist winds from Sea regions behind weather shift Lucknow-based meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said- Moist winds arriving from the Bay of Bengal and the Arabian Sea have altered weather conditions across Uttar Pradesh. Thunderstorms and rainfall have been occurring due to an active western disturbance since May 28. Its impact is expected to continue until June 1. He added that western Uttar Pradesh and the Terai belt face the highest risk of storms. Weather conditions are expected to change again from June 2, leading to a rise in temperatures. However, heatwave conditions are not expected for now. How will the weather be over the next five days? June 1- Scattered showers are likely at several places in western Uttar Pradesh and at isolated locations in eastern Uttar Pradesh. June 2- Weather is expected to remain clear across the state. The absence of heatwave conditions will continue to provide relief from extreme heat. June 3- Skies will remain clear across Uttar Pradesh. Temperatures will rise, and warmer conditions will return. June 4- Clear skies are expected in both eastern and western Uttar Pradesh. Hot winds will blow, and the heat is likely to intensify once again. June 5- Light rainfall is possible in western Uttar Pradesh, while eastern Uttar Pradesh is expected to remain dry. Hot weather conditions are likely to persist.
